25010.label: Luke 1:1
25010.text: Whereas many have undertaken to compile a statement of the facts that are given full credence among us,

25011.label: Luke 1:2
25011.text: just as those who from [the] beginning became eyewitnesses and attendants of the message delivered these to us,

25012.label: Luke 1:3
25012.text: I resolved also, because I have traced all things from the start with accuracy, to write them in logical order to you, most excellent The·ophʹi·lus,

25013.label: Luke 1:4
25013.text: that you may know fully the certainty of the things that you have been taught orally.

25014.label: Luke 1:5
25014.text: In the days of Herod, king of Ju·deʹa, there happened to be a certain priest named Zech·a·riʹah of the division of A·biʹjah, and he had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

25015.label: Luke 1:6
25015.text: They both were righteous before God because of walking blamelessly in accord with all the commandments and legal requirements of Jehovah.

25016.label: Luke 1:7
25016.text: But they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well along in years.

25017.label: Luke 1:8
25017.text: Now as he was acting as priest in the assignment of his division before God,

25018.label: Luke 1:9
25018.text: according to the solemn practice of the priestly office it became his turn to offer incense when he entered into the sanctuary of Jehovah;

25019.label: Luke 1:10
25019.text: and all the multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of offering incense.

25020.label: Luke 1:11
25020.text: To him Jehovah’s angel appeared, standing at the right side of the incense altar.

25021.label: Luke 1:12
25021.text: But Zech·a·riʹah became troubled at the sight, and fear fell upon him.

25022.label: Luke 1:13
25022.text: However, the angel said to him: “Have no fear, Zech·a·riʹah, because your supplication has been favorably heard, and your wife Elizabeth will become mother to a son to you, and you are to call his name John.

25023.label: Luke 1:14
25023.text: And you will have joy and great gladness, and many will rejoice over his birth;

25024.label: Luke 1:15
25024.text: for he will be great before Jehovah. But he must drink no wine and strong drink at all, and he will be filled with holy spirit right from his mother’s womb;

25025.label: Luke 1:16
25025.text: and many of the sons of Israel will he turn back to Jehovah their God.

25026.label: Luke 1:17
25026.text: Also, he will go before him with E·liʹjah’s spirit and power, to turn back the hearts of fathers to children and the disobedient ones to the practical wisdom of righteous ones, to get ready for Jehovah a prepared people.”

25027.label: Luke 1:18
25027.text: And Zech·a·riʹah said to the angel: “How am I to be sure of this? For I am aged and my wife is well along in years.”

25028.label: Luke 1:19
25028.text: In reply the angel said to him: “I am Gaʹbri·el, who stands near before God, and I was sent forth to speak with you and declare the good news of these things to you.

25029.label: Luke 1:20
25029.text: But, look! you will be silent and not able to speak until the day that these things take place, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their appointed time.”

25030.label: Luke 1:21
25030.text: Meanwhile the people continued waiting for Zech·a·riʹah, and they began to wonder at his delaying in the sanctuary.

25031.label: Luke 1:22
25031.text: But when he came out he was not able to speak to them, and they perceived that he had just seen a supernatural sight in the sanctuary; and he kept making signs to them, but remained dumb.

25032.label: Luke 1:23
25032.text: When, now, the days of his public service were fulfilled, he went off to his home.

25033.label: Luke 1:24
25033.text: But after these days Elizabeth his wife became pregnant; and she kept herself secluded for five months, saying:

25034.label: Luke 1:25
25034.text: “This is the way Jehovah has dealt with me in these days when he has given me his attention to take away my reproach among men.”

25035.label: Luke 1:26
25035.text: In her sixth month the angel Gaʹbri·el was sent forth from God to a city of Galʹi·lee named Nazʹa·reth,

25036.label: Luke 1:27
25036.text: to a virgin promised in marriage to a man named Joseph of David’s house; and the name of the virgin was Mary.

25037.label: Luke 1:28
25037.text: And when he went in before her he said: “Good day, highly favored one, Jehovah is with you.”

25038.label: Luke 1:29
25038.text: But she was deeply disturbed at the saying and began to reason out what sort of greeting this might be.

25039.label: Luke 1:30
25039.text: So the angel said to her: “Have no fear, Mary, for you have found favor with God;

25040.label: Luke 1:31
25040.text: and, look! you will conceive in your womb and give birth to a son, and you are to call his name Jesus.

25041.label: Luke 1:32
25041.text: This one will be great and will be called Son of the Most High; and Jehovah God will give him the throne of David his father,

25042.label: Luke 1:33
25042.text: and he will rule as king over the house of Jacob forever, and there will be no end of his kingdom.”

25043.label: Luke 1:34
25043.text: But Mary said to the angel: “How is this to be, since I am having no intercourse with a man?”

25044.label: Luke 1:35
25044.text: In answer the angel said to her: “Holy spirit will come upon you, and power of the Most High will overshadow you. For that reason also what is born will be called holy, God’s Son.

25045.label: Luke 1:36
25045.text: And, look! Elizabeth your relative has also herself conceived a son, in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her, the so-called barren woman;

25046.label: Luke 1:37
25046.text: because with God no declaration will be an impossibility.”

25047.label: Luke 1:38
25047.text: Then Mary said: “Look! Jehovah’s slave girl! May it take place with me according to your declaration.” At that the angel departed from her.

25048.label: Luke 1:39
25048.text: So Mary rose in these days and went into the mountainous country with haste, to a city of Judah,

25049.label: Luke 1:40
25049.text: and she entered into the home of Zech·a·riʹah and greeted Elizabeth.

25050.label: Luke 1:41
25050.text: Well, as Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the infant in her womb leaped; and Elizabeth was filled with holy spirit,

25051.label: Luke 1:42
25051.text: and she called out with a loud cry and said: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!

25052.label: Luke 1:43
25052.text: So how is it that this [privilege] is mine, to have the mother of my Lord come to me?

25053.label: Luke 1:44
25053.text: For, look! as the sound of your greeting fell upon my ears, the infant in my womb leaped with great gladness.

25054.label: Luke 1:45
25054.text: Happy too is she that believed, because there will be a complete performance of those things spoken to her from Jehovah.”

25055.label: Luke 1:46
25055.text: And Mary said: “My soul magnifies Jehovah,

25056.label: Luke 1:47
25056.text: and my spirit cannot keep from being overjoyed at God my Savior;

25057.label: Luke 1:48
25057.text: because he has looked upon the low position of his slave girl. For, look! from now on all generations will pronounce me happy;

25058.label: Luke 1:49
25058.text: because the powerful One has done great deeds for me, and holy is his name;

25059.label: Luke 1:50
25059.text: and for generations after generations his mercy is upon those who fear him.

25060.label: Luke 1:51
25060.text: He has performed mightily with his arm, he has scattered abroad those who are haughty in the intention of their hearts.

25061.label: Luke 1:52
25061.text: He has brought down men of power from thrones and exalted lowly ones;

25062.label: Luke 1:53
25062.text: he has fully satisfied hungry ones with good things and he has sent away empty those who had wealth.

25063.label: Luke 1:54
25063.text: He has come to the aid of Israel his servant, to call to mind mercy,

25064.label: Luke 1:55
25064.text: just as he told to our forefathers, to Abraham and to his seed, forever.”

25065.label: Luke 1:56
25065.text: Then Mary remained with her about three months, and returned to her own home.

25066.label: Luke 1:57
25066.text: The time now became due for Elizabeth to give birth, and she became mother to a son.

25067.label: Luke 1:58
25067.text: And the neighbors and her relatives heard that Jehovah had magnified his mercy to her, and they began to rejoice with her.

25068.label: Luke 1:59
25068.text: And on the eighth day they came to circumcise the young child, and they were going to call it by the name of its father, Zech·a·riʹah.

25069.label: Luke 1:60
25069.text: But its mother answered and said: “No, indeed! but he shall be called John.”

25070.label: Luke 1:61
25070.text: At this they said to her: “There is no one among your relatives that is called by this name.”

25071.label: Luke 1:62
25071.text: Then they went asking its father by signs what he wanted it to be called.

25072.label: Luke 1:63
25072.text: And he asked for a tablet and wrote: “John is its name.” At this they all marveled.

25073.label: Luke 1:64
25073.text: Instantly his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed and he began to speak, blessing God.

25074.label: Luke 1:65
25074.text: And fear fell upon all those living in their neighborhood; and in the whole mountainous country of Ju·deʹa all these things began to be talked around,

25075.label: Luke 1:66
25075.text: and all that heard made note of it in their hearts, saying: “What really will this young child be?” For the hand of Jehovah was indeed with it.

25076.label: Luke 1:67
25076.text: And Zech·a·riʹah its father was filled with holy spirit, and he prophesied, saying:

25077.label: Luke 1:68
25077.text: “Blessed be Jehovah the God of Israel, because he has turned his attention and performed deliverance toward his people.

25078.label: Luke 1:69
25078.text: And he has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,

25079.label: Luke 1:70
25079.text: just as he, through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old, has spoken

25080.label: Luke 1:71
25080.text: of a salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all those hating us;

25081.label: Luke 1:72
25081.text: to perform the mercy in connection with our forefathers and to call to mind his holy covenant,

25082.label: Luke 1:73
25082.text: the oath that he swore to Abraham our forefather,

25083.label: Luke 1:74
25083.text: to grant us, after we have been rescued from the hands of enemies, the privilege of fearlessly rendering sacred service to him

25084.label: Luke 1:75
25084.text: with loyalty and righteousness before him all our days.

25085.label: Luke 1:76
25085.text: But as for you, young child, you will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go in advance before Jehovah to make his ways ready,

25086.label: Luke 1:77
25086.text: to give knowledge of salvation to his people by forgiveness of their sins,

25087.label: Luke 1:78
25087.text: because of the tender compassion of our God. With this [compassion] a daybreak will visit us from on high,

25088.label: Luke 1:79
25088.text: to give light to those sitting in darkness and death’s shadow, to direct our feet prosperously in the way of peace.”

25089.label: Luke 1:80
25089.text: And the young child went on growing and getting strong in spirit, and he continued in the deserts until the day of showing himself openly to Israel.

25090.label: Luke 2:1
25090.text: Now in those days a decree went forth from Caesar Au·gusʹtus for all the inhabited earth to be registered;

25091.label: Luke 2:2
25091.text: (this first registration took place when Qui·rinʹi·us was governor of Syria;)

25092.label: Luke 2:3
25092.text: and all people went traveling to be registered, each one to his own city.

25093.label: Luke 2:4
25093.text: Of course, Joseph also went up from Galʹi·lee, out of the city of Nazʹa·reth, into Ju·deʹa, to David’s city, which is called Bethʹle·hem, because of his being a member of the house and family of David,

25094.label: Luke 2:5
25094.text: to get registered with Mary, who had been given him in marriage as promised, at present heavy with child.

25095.label: Luke 2:6
25095.text: While they were there, the days came to the full for her to give birth.

25096.label: Luke 2:7
25096.text: And she gave birth to her son, the firstborn, and she bound him with cloth bands and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging room.

25097.label: Luke 2:8
25097.text: There were also in that same country shepherds living out of doors and keeping watches in the night over their flocks.

25098.label: Luke 2:9
25098.text: And suddenly Jehovah’s angel stood by them, and Jehovah’s glory gleamed around them, and they became very fearful.

25099.label: Luke 2:10
25099.text: But the angel said to them: “Have no fear, for, look! I am declaring to YOU good news of a great joy that all the people will have,

25100.label: Luke 2:11
25100.text: because there was born to YOU today a Savior, who is Christ [the] Lord, in David’s city.

25101.label: Luke 2:12
25101.text: And this is a sign for YOU: YOU will find an infant bound in cloth bands and lying in a manger.”

25102.label: Luke 2:13
25102.text: And suddenly there came to be with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying:

25103.label: Luke 2:14
25103.text: “Glory in the heights above to God, and upon earth peace among men of goodwill.”

25104.label: Luke 2:15
25104.text: So when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the shepherds began saying to one another: “Let us by all means go clear to Bethʹle·hem and see this thing that has taken place, which Jehovah has made known to us.”

25105.label: Luke 2:16
25105.text: And they went with haste and found Mary as well as Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

25106.label: Luke 2:17
25106.text: When they saw it, they made known the saying that had been spoken to them concerning this young child.

25107.label: Luke 2:18
25107.text: And all that heard marveled over the things told them by the shepherds,

25108.label: Luke 2:19
25108.text: but Mary began to preserve all these sayings, drawing conclusions in her heart.

25109.label: Luke 2:20
25109.text: Then the shepherds went back, glorifying and praising God for all the things they heard and saw, just as these had been told them.

25110.label: Luke 2:21
25110.text: Now when eight days came to the full for circumcising him, his name was also called Jesus, the name called by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

25111.label: Luke 2:22
25111.text: Also, when the days for purifying them according to the law of Moses came to the full, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to Jehovah,

25112.label: Luke 2:23
25112.text: just as it is written in Jehovah’s law: “Every male opening a womb must be called holy to Jehovah,”

25113.label: Luke 2:24
25113.text: and to offer sacrifice according to what is said in the law of Jehovah: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

25114.label: Luke 2:25
25114.text: And, look! there was a man in Jerusalem named Simʹe·on, and this man was righteous and reverent, waiting for Israel’s consolation, and holy spirit was upon him.

25115.label: Luke 2:26
25115.text: Furthermore, it had been divinely revealed to him by the holy spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Christ of Jehovah.

25116.label: Luke 2:27
25116.text: Under the power of the spirit he now came into the temple; and as the parents brought the young child Jesus in to do for it according to the customary practice of the law,

25117.label: Luke 2:28
25117.text: he himself received it into his arms and blessed God and said:

25118.label: Luke 2:29
25118.text: “Now, Sovereign Lord, you are letting your slave go free in peace according to your declaration;

25119.label: Luke 2:30
25119.text: because my eyes have seen your means of saving

25120.label: Luke 2:31
25120.text: that you have made ready in the sight of all the peoples,

25121.label: Luke 2:32
25121.text: a light for removing the veil from the nations and a glory of your people Israel.”

25122.label: Luke 2:33
25122.text: And its father and mother continued wondering at the things being spoken about it.

25123.label: Luke 2:34
25123.text: Also, Simʹe·on blessed them, but said to Mary its mother: “Look! This one is laid for the fall and the rising again of many in Israel and for a sign to be talked against

25124.label: Luke 2:35
25124.text: (yes, a long sword will be run through the soul of you yourself), in order that the reasonings of many hearts may be uncovered.”

25125.label: Luke 2:36
25125.text: Now there was Anna a prophetess, Phanʹu·el’s daughter, of Ashʹer’s tribe (this woman was well along in years, and had lived with a husband for seven years from her virginity,

25126.label: Luke 2:37
25126.text: and she was a widow now eighty-four years old), who was never missing from the temple, rendering sacred service night and day with fastings and supplications.

25127.label: Luke 2:38
25127.text: And in that very hour she came near and began returning thanks to God and speaking about [the child] to all those waiting for Jerusalem’s deliverance.

25128.label: Luke 2:39
25128.text: So when they had carried out all the things according to the law of Jehovah, they went back into Galʹi·lee to their own city Nazʹa·reth.

25129.label: Luke 2:40
25129.text: And the young child continued growing and getting strong, being filled with wisdom, and God’s favor continued upon him.

25130.label: Luke 2:41
25130.text: Now his parents were accustomed to go from year to year to Jerusalem for the festival of the passover.

25131.label: Luke 2:42
25131.text: And when he became twelve years old, they went up according to the custom of the festival

25132.label: Luke 2:43
25132.text: and completed the days. But when they were returning, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and his parents did not notice it.

25133.label: Luke 2:44
25133.text: Assuming that he was in the company traveling together, they covered a day’s distance and then began to hunt him up among the relatives and acquaintances.

25134.label: Luke 2:45
25134.text: But, not finding him, they returned to Jerusalem, making a diligent search for him.

25135.label: Luke 2:46
25135.text: Well, after three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers and listening to them and questioning them.

25136.label: Luke 2:47
25136.text: But all those listening to him were in constant amazement at his understanding and his answers.

25137.label: Luke 2:48
25137.text: Now when they saw him they were astounded, and his mother said to him: “Child, why did you treat us this way? Here your father and I in mental distress have been looking for you.”

25138.label: Luke 2:49
25138.text: But he said to them: “Why did YOU have to go looking for me? Did YOU not know that I must be in the [house] of my Father?”

25139.label: Luke 2:50
25139.text: However, they did not grasp the saying that he spoke to them.

25140.label: Luke 2:51
25140.text: And he went down with them and came to Nazʹa·reth, and he continued subject to them. Also, his mother carefully kept all these sayings in her heart.

25141.label: Luke 2:52
25141.text: And Jesus went on progressing in wisdom and in physical growth and in favor with God and men.

25142.label: Luke 3:1
25142.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Ti·beʹri·us Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Ju·deʹa, and Herod was district ruler of Galʹi·lee, but Philip his brother was district ruler of the country of It·u·raeʹa and Trach·o·niʹtis, and Ly·saʹni·as was district ruler of Ab·i·leʹne,

25143.label: Luke 3:2
25143.text: in the days of chief priest Anʹnas and of Caʹia·phas, God’s declaration came to John the son of Zech·a·riʹah in the wilderness.

25144.label: Luke 3:3
25144.text: So he came into all the country around the Jordan, preaching baptism [in symbol] of repentance for forgiveness of sins,

25145.label: Luke 3:4
25145.text: just as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “Listen! Someone is crying out in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of Jehovah, YOU people, make his roads straight.

25146.label: Luke 3:5
25146.text: Every gully must be filled up, and every mountain and hill leveled down, and the curves must become straight ways and the rough places smooth ways;

25147.label: Luke 3:6
25147.text: and all flesh will see the saving means of God.’”

25148.label: Luke 3:7
25148.text: Therefore he began to say to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him: “YOU offspring of vipers, who has intimated to YOU to flee from the coming wrath?

25149.label: Luke 3:8
25149.text: Therefore produce fruits that befit repentance. And do not start saying within yourselves, ‘As a father we have Abraham.’ For I say to YOU that God has power to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.

25150.label: Luke 3:9
25150.text: Indeed, the ax is already in position at the root of the trees; every tree, therefore, not producing fine fruit is to be cut down and thrown into the fire.”

25151.label: Luke 3:10
25151.text: And the crowds would ask him: “What, then, shall we do?”

25152.label: Luke 3:11
25152.text: In reply he would say to them: “Let the man that has two undergarments share with the man that has none, and let him that has things to eat do the same.”

25153.label: Luke 3:12
25153.text: But even tax collectors came to be baptized, and they said to him: “Teacher, what shall we do?”

25154.label: Luke 3:13
25154.text: He said to them: “Do not demand anything more than the tax rate.”

25155.label: Luke 3:14
25155.text: Also, those in military service would ask him: “What shall we also do?” And he said to them: “Do not harass anybody or accuse anybody falsely, but be satisfied with YOUR provisions.”

25156.label: Luke 3:15
25156.text: Now as the people were in expectation and all were reasoning in their hearts about John: “May he perhaps be the Christ?”

25157.label: Luke 3:16
25157.text: John gave the answer, saying to all: “I, for my part, baptize YOU with water; but the one stronger than I am is coming, the lace of whose sandals I am not fit to untie. He will baptize YOU people with holy spirit and fire.

25158.label: Luke 3:17
25158.text: His winnowing shovel is in his hand to clean up his threshing floor completely and to gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he will burn up with fire that cannot be put out.”

25159.label: Luke 3:18
25159.text: Therefore he also gave many other exhortations and continued declaring good news to the people.

25160.label: Luke 3:19
25160.text: But Herod the district ruler, for being reproved by him concerning He·roʹdi·as the wife of his brother and concerning all the wicked deeds that Herod did,

25161.label: Luke 3:20
25161.text: added also this to all those [deeds]: he locked John up in prison.

25162.label: Luke 3:21
25162.text: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also was baptized and, as he was praying, the heaven was opened up

25163.label: Luke 3:22
25163.text: and the holy spirit in bodily shape like a dove came down upon him, and a voice came out of heaven: “You are my Son, the beloved; I have approved you.”

25164.label: Luke 3:23
25164.text: Furthermore, Jesus himself, when he commenced [his work], was about thirty years old, being the son, as the opinion was, of Joseph, [son] of Heʹli,

25165.label: Luke 3:24
25165.text: [son] of Matʹthat,[son] of Leʹvi,[son] of Melʹchi,[son] of Janʹna·i,[son] of Joseph,

25166.label: Luke 3:25
25166.text: [son] of Mat·ta·thiʹas,[son] of Aʹmos,[son] of Naʹhum,[son] of Esʹli,[son] of Nagʹga·i,

25167.label: Luke 3:26
25167.text: [son] of Maʹath,[son] of Mat·ta·thiʹas,[son] of Semʹe·in,[son] of Joʹsech,[son] of Joʹda,

25168.label: Luke 3:27
25168.text: [son] of Jo·anʹan,[son] of Rheʹsa,[son] of Ze·rubʹba·bel, [son] of She·alʹti·el, [son] of Neʹri,

25169.label: Luke 3:28
25169.text: [son] of Melʹchi,[son] of Adʹdi,[son] of Coʹsam,[son] of El·maʹdam,[son] of Er,

25170.label: Luke 3:29
25170.text: [son] of Jesus, [son] of E·li·eʹzer,[son] of Joʹrim,[son] of Matʹthat,[son] of Leʹvi,

25171.label: Luke 3:30
25171.text: [son] of Symʹe·on,[son] of Judas,[son] of Joseph,[son] of Joʹnam,[son] of E·liʹa·kim,

25172.label: Luke 3:31
25172.text: [son] of Meʹle·a,[son] of Menʹna,[son] of Matʹta·tha,[son] of Nathan, [son] of David,

25173.label: Luke 3:32
25173.text: [son] of Jesʹse, [son] of Oʹbed, [son] of Boʹaz, [son] of Salʹmon, [son] of Nahʹshon,

25174.label: Luke 3:33
25174.text: [son] of Am·minʹa·dab, [son] of Arʹni, [son] of Hezʹron, [son] of Peʹrez, [son] of Judah,

25175.label: Luke 3:34
25175.text: [son] of Jacob, [son] of Isaac, [son] of Abraham, [son] of Teʹrah, [son] of Naʹhor,

25176.label: Luke 3:35
25176.text: [son] of Seʹrug, [son] of Reʹu, [son] of Peʹleg, [son] of Eʹber, [son] of Sheʹlah,

25177.label: Luke 3:36
25177.text: [son] of Ca·iʹnan, [son] of Ar·pachʹshad, [son] of Shem, [son] of Noah, [son] of Laʹmech,

25178.label: Luke 3:37
25178.text: [son] of Me·thuʹse·lah, [son] of Eʹnoch, [son] of Jaʹred, [son] of Ma·haʹla·le·el, [son] of Ca·iʹnan,

25179.label: Luke 3:38
25179.text: [son] of Eʹnosh, [son] of Seth, [son] of Adam, [son] of God.

25180.label: Luke 4:1
25180.text: Now Jesus, full of holy spirit, turned away from the Jordan, and he was led about by the spirit in the wilderness

25181.label: Luke 4:2
25181.text: for forty days, while being tempted by the Devil. Furthermore, he ate nothing in those days, and so, when they were concluded, he felt hungry.

25182.label: Luke 4:3
25182.text: At this the Devil said to him: “If you are a son of God, tell this stone to become a loaf of bread.”

25183.label: Luke 4:4
25183.text: But Jesus replied to him: “It is written, ‘Man must not live by bread alone.’”

25184.label: Luke 4:5
25184.text: So he brought him up and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited earth in an instant of time;

25185.label: Luke 4:6
25185.text: and the Devil said to him: “I will give you all this authority and the glory of them, because it has been delivered to me, and to whomever I wish I give it.

25186.label: Luke 4:7
25186.text: You, therefore, if you do an act of worship before me, it will all be yours.”

25187.label: Luke 4:8
25187.text: In reply Jesus said to him: “It is written, ‘It is Jehovah your God you must worship, and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.’”

25188.label: Luke 4:9
25188.text: Now he led him into Jerusalem and stationed him upon the battlement of the temple and said to him: “If you are a son of God, hurl yourself down from here;

25189.label: Luke 4:10
25189.text: for it is written, ‘He will give his angels a charge concerning you, to preserve you,’

25190.label: Luke 4:11
25190.text: and, ‘They will carry you on their hands, that you may at no time strike your foot against a stone.’”

25191.label: Luke 4:12
25191.text: In answer Jesus said to him: “It is said, ‘You must not put Jehovah your God to the test.’”

25192.label: Luke 4:13
25192.text: So the Devil, having concluded all the temptation, retired from him until another convenient time.

25193.label: Luke 4:14
25193.text: Now Jesus returned in the power of the spirit into Galʹi·lee. And good talk concerning him spread out through all the surrounding country.

25194.label: Luke 4:15
25194.text: Also, he began to teach in their synagogues, being held in honor by all.

25195.label: Luke 4:16
25195.text: And he came to Nazʹa·reth, where he had been reared; and, according to his custom on the sabbath day, he entered into the synagogue, and he stood up to read.

25196.label: Luke 4:17
25196.text: So the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed him, and he opened the scroll and found the place where it was written:

25197.label: Luke 4:18
25197.text: “Jehovah’s spirit is upon me, because he anointed me to declare good news to the poor, he sent me forth to preach a release to the captives and a recovery of sight to the blind, to send the crushed ones away with a release,

25199.label: Luke 4:20
25199.text: With that he rolled up the scroll, handed it back to the attendant and sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were intently fixed upon him.

25200.label: Luke 4:21
25200.text: Then he started to say to them: “Today this scripture that YOU just heard is fulfilled.”

25201.label: Luke 4:22
25201.text: And they all began to give favorable witness about him and to marvel at the winsome words proceeding out of his mouth, and they were saying: “This is a son of Joseph, is it not?”

25202.label: Luke 4:23
25202.text: At this he said to them: “No doubt YOU will apply this illustration to me, ‘Physician, cure yourself; the things we heard as having happened in Ca·perʹna·um do also here in your home territory.’”

25203.label: Luke 4:24
25203.text: But he said: “Truly I tell YOU that no prophet is accepted in his home territory.

25204.label: Luke 4:25
25204.text: For instance, I tell YOU in truth, There were many widows in Israel in the days of E·liʹjah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, so that a great famine fell upon all the land,

25205.label: Luke 4:26
25205.text: yet E·liʹjah was sent to none of those [women], but only to Zarʹe·phath in the land of Siʹdon to a widow.

25206.label: Luke 4:27
25206.text: Also, there were many lepers in Israel in the time of E·liʹsha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed, but Naʹa·man the man of Syria.”

25207.label: Luke 4:28
25207.text: Now all those hearing these things in the synagogue became filled with anger;

25208.label: Luke 4:29
25208.text: and they rose up and hurried him outside the city, and they led him to the brow of the mountain upon which their city had been built, in order to throw him down headlong.

25209.label: Luke 4:30
25209.text: But he went through the midst of them and continued on his way.

25210.label: Luke 4:31
25210.text: And he went down to Ca·perʹna·um, a city of Galʹi·lee. And he was teaching them on the sabbath;

25211.label: Luke 4:32
25211.text: and they were astounded at his way of teaching, because his speech was with authority.

25212.label: Luke 4:33
25212.text: Now in the synagogue there was a man with a spirit, an unclean demon, and he shouted with a loud voice:

25213.label: Luke 4:34
25213.text: “Ah! What have we to do with you, Jesus you Naz·a·reneʹ? Did you come to destroy us? I know exactly who you are, the Holy One of God.”

25214.label: Luke 4:35
25214.text: But Jesus rebuked it, saying: “Be silent, and come out of him.” So, after throwing the man down in their midst, the demon came out of him without hurting him.

25215.label: Luke 4:36
25215.text: At this, astonishment fell upon all, and they began to converse with one another, saying: “What sort of speech is this, because with authority and power he orders the unclean spirits, and out they come?”

25216.label: Luke 4:37
25216.text: So the news concerning him kept going out into every corner of the surrounding country.

25217.label: Luke 4:38
25217.text: After getting up out of the synagogue he entered into Simon’s home. Now Simon’s mother-in-law was distressed with a high fever, and they made request of him for her.

25218.label: Luke 4:39
25218.text: So he stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Instantly she rose and began ministering to them.

25219.label: Luke 4:40
25219.text: But when the sun was setting, all those who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. By laying his hands upon each one of them he would cure them.

25220.label: Luke 4:41
25220.text: Demons also would come out of many, crying out and saying: “You are the Son of God.” But, rebuking them, he would not permit them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.

25221.label: Luke 4:42
25221.text: However, when it became day, he went out and proceeded to a lonely place. But the crowds began hunting about for him and came out as far as he was, and they tried to detain him from going away from them.

25222.label: Luke 4:43
25222.text: But he said to them: “Also to other cities I must declare the good news of the kingdom of God, because for this I was sent forth.”

25223.label: Luke 4:44
25223.text: Accordingly he went on preaching in the synagogues of Ju·deʹa.

25224.label: Luke 5:1
25224.text: On an occasion when the crowd was pressing close upon him and listening to the word of God, he was standing beside the lake of Gen·nesʹa·ret.

25225.label: Luke 5:2
25225.text: And he saw two boats docked at the lakeside, but the fishermen had got out of them and were washing off their nets.

25226.label: Luke 5:3
25226.text: Going aboard one of the boats, which was Simon’s, he asked him to pull away a bit from land. Then he sat down, and from the boat he began teaching the crowds.

25227.label: Luke 5:4
25227.text: When he ceased speaking, he said to Simon: “Pull out to where it is deep, and YOU men let down YOUR nets for a catch.”

25228.label: Luke 5:5
25228.text: But Simon in reply said: “Instructor, for a whole night we toiled and took nothing, but at your bidding I will lower the nets.”

25229.label: Luke 5:6
25229.text: Well, when they did this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish. In fact, their nets began ripping apart.

25230.label: Luke 5:7
25230.text: So they motioned to their partners in the other boat to come and assist them; and they did come, and they filled both boats, so that these began to sink.

25231.label: Luke 5:8
25231.text: Seeing this, Simon Peter fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying: “Depart from me, because I am a sinful man, Lord.”

25232.label: Luke 5:9
25232.text: For at the catch of fish which they took up astonishment overwhelmed him and all those with him,

25233.label: Luke 5:10
25233.text: and likewise both James and John, Zebʹe·dee’s sons, who were sharers with Simon. But Jesus said to Simon: “Stop being afraid. From now on you will be catching men alive.”

25234.label: Luke 5:11
25234.text: So they brought the boats back to land, and abandoned everything and followed him.

25235.label: Luke 5:12
25235.text: On a further occasion while he was in one of the cities, look! a man full of leprosy! When he caught sight of Jesus he fell upon his face and begged him, saying: “Lord, if you just want to, you can make me clean.”

25236.label: Luke 5:13
25236.text: And so, stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: “I want to. Be made clean.” And immediately the leprosy vanished from him.

25237.label: Luke 5:14
25237.text: And he gave the man orders to tell nobody: “But go off and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering in connection with your cleansing, just as Moses directed, for a witness to them.”

25238.label: Luke 5:15
25238.text: But the word about him was spreading the more, and great crowds would come together to listen and to be cured of their sicknesses.

25239.label: Luke 5:16
25239.text: However, he continued in retirement in the deserts and praying.

25240.label: Luke 5:17
25240.text: In the course of one of the days he was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law who had come out of every village of Galʹi·lee and Ju·deʹa and Jerusalem were sitting there; and Jehovah’s power was there for him to do healing.

25241.label: Luke 5:18
25241.text: And, look! men carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were seeking a way to bring him in and place him before him.

25242.label: Luke 5:19
25242.text: So, not finding a way to bring him in on account of the crowd, they climbed up to the roof, and through the tiling they let him down with the little bed among those in front of Jesus.

25243.label: Luke 5:20
25243.text: And when he saw their faith he said: “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”

25244.label: Luke 5:21
25244.text: Thereupon the scribes and the Pharisees started to reason, saying: “Who is this that is speaking blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”

25245.label: Luke 5:22
25245.text: But Jesus, discerning their reasonings, said in answer to them: “What are YOU reasoning out in YOUR hearts?

25246.label: Luke 5:23
25246.text: Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?

25247.label: Luke 5:24
25247.text: But in order for YOU to know that the Son of man has authority on the earth to forgive sins—” he said to the paralyzed man: “I say to you, Get up and pick up your little bed and be on your way home.”

25248.label: Luke 5:25
25248.text: And instantly he rose up before them, picked up what he used to lie on and went off to his home, glorifying God.

25249.label: Luke 5:26
25249.text: Then an ecstasy seized one and all, and they began to glorify God, and they became filled with fear, saying: “We have seen strange things today!”

25250.label: Luke 5:27
25250.text: Now after these things he went out and beheld a tax collector named Leʹvi sitting at the tax office, and he said to him: “Be my follower.”

25251.label: Luke 5:28
25251.text: And leaving everything behind he rose up and went following him.

25252.label: Luke 5:29
25252.text: Also, Leʹvi spread a big reception feast for him in his house; and there was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were with them reclining at the meal.

25253.label: Luke 5:30
25253.text: At this the Pharisees and their scribes began murmuring to his disciples, saying: “Why is it YOU eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

25254.label: Luke 5:31
25254.text: In reply Jesus said to them: “Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are ailing do.

25255.label: Luke 5:32
25255.text: I have come to call, not righteous persons, but sinners to repentance.”

25256.label: Luke 5:33
25256.text: They said to him: “The disciples of John fast frequently and offer supplications, and so do those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink.”

25257.label: Luke 5:34
25257.text: Jesus said to them: “YOU cannot make the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them, can YOU?

25258.label: Luke 5:35
25258.text: Yet days will come when the bridegroom will indeed be taken away from them; then they will fast in those days.”

25259.label: Luke 5:36
25259.text: Further, he went on to give an illustration to them: “No one cuts a patch from a new outer garment and sews it onto an old outer garment; but if he does, then both the new patch tears away and the patch from the new garment does not match the old.

25260.label: Luke 5:37
25260.text: Moreover, no one puts new wine into old wineskins; but if he does, then the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled out and the wineskins will be ruined.

25261.label: Luke 5:38
25261.text: But new wine must be put into new wineskins.

25262.label: Luke 5:39
25262.text: No one that has drunk old wine wants new; for he says, ‘The old is nice.’”

25263.label: Luke 6:1
25263.text: Now on a sabbath he happened to be passing through grainfields, and his disciples were plucking and eating the heads of grain, rubbing them with their hands.

25264.label: Luke 6:2
25264.text: At this some of the Pharisees said: “Why are YOU doing what is not lawful on the sabbath?”

25265.label: Luke 6:3
25265.text: But Jesus said in reply to them: “Have YOU never read the very thing David did when he and the men with him got hungry?

25266.label: Luke 6:4
25266.text: How he entered into the house of God and received the loaves of presentation and ate and gave some to the men with him, which it is lawful for no one to eat but for the priests only?”

25267.label: Luke 6:5
25267.text: And he went on to say to them: “Lord of the sabbath is what the Son of man is.”

25268.label: Luke 6:6
25268.text: In the course of another sabbath he entered into the synagogue and began teaching. And there was a man present whose right hand was withered.

25269.label: Luke 6:7
25269.text: The scribes and the Pharisees were now watching him closely to see whether he would cure on the sabbath, in order to find some way to accuse him.

25270.label: Luke 6:8
25270.text: He, however, knew their reasonings, yet he said to the man with the withered hand: “Get up and stand in the center.” And he rose and took his stand.

25271.label: Luke 6:9
25271.text: Then Jesus said to them: “I ask YOU men, Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do injury, to save or to destroy a soul?”

25272.label: Luke 6:10
25272.text: And after looking around at them all, he said to the man: “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and his hand was restored.

25273.label: Luke 6:11
25273.text: But they became filled with madness, and they began to talk over with one another what they might do to Jesus.

25274.label: Luke 6:12
25274.text: In the progress of these days he went out into the mountain to pray, and he continued the whole night in prayer to God.

25275.label: Luke 6:13
25275.text: But when it became day he called his disciples to him and chose from among them twelve, whom he also named apostles:

25276.label: Luke 6:14
25276.text: Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John, and Philip and Bar·tholʹo·mew,

25277.label: Luke 6:15
25277.text: and Matthew and Thomas, and James [the son] of Al·phaeʹus, and Simon who is called “the zealous one,”

25278.label: Luke 6:16
25278.text: and Judas [the son] of James, and Judas Is·carʹi·ot, who turned traitor.

25279.label: Luke 6:17
25279.text: And he came down with them and took his station on a level place, and there was a great crowd of his disciples, and a great multitude of people from all of Ju·deʹa and Jerusalem and the maritime country of Tyre and Siʹdon, who came to hear him and be healed of their sicknesses.

25280.label: Luke 6:18
25280.text: Even those troubled with unclean spirits were cured.

25281.label: Luke 6:19
25281.text: And all the crowd were seeking to touch him, because power was going out of him and healing them all.

25282.label: Luke 6:20
25282.text: And he lifted up his eyes upon his disciples and began to say: “Happy are YOU poor, because YOURS is the kingdom of God.

25283.label: Luke 6:21
25283.text: “Happy are YOU who hunger now, because YOU will be filled. “Happy are YOU who weep now, because YOU will laugh.

25284.label: Luke 6:22
25284.text: “Happy are YOU whenever men hate YOU, and whenever they exclude YOU and reproach YOU and cast out YOUR name as wicked for the sake of the Son of man.

25285.label: Luke 6:23
25285.text: Rejoice in that day and leap, for, look! YOUR reward is great in heaven, for those are the same things their forefathers used to do to the prophets.

25286.label: Luke 6:24
25286.text: “But woe to YOU rich persons, because YOU are having YOUR consolation in full.

25287.label: Luke 6:25
25287.text: “Woe to YOU who are filled up now, because YOU will go hungry. “Woe, YOU who are laughing now, because YOU will mourn and weep.

25288.label: Luke 6:26
25288.text: “Woe, whenever all men speak well of YOU, for things like these are what their forefathers did to the false prophets.

25289.label: Luke 6:27
25289.text: “But I say to YOU who are listening, Continue to love YOUR enemies, to do good to those hating YOU,

25290.label: Luke 6:28
25290.text: to bless those cursing YOU, to pray for those who are insulting YOU.

25291.label: Luke 6:29
25291.text: To him that strikes you on the one cheek, offer the other also; and from him that takes away your outer garment, do not withhold even the undergarment.

25292.label: Luke 6:30
25292.text: Give to everyone asking you, and from the one taking your things away do not ask [them] back.

25293.label: Luke 6:31
25293.text: “Also, just as YOU want men to do to YOU, do the same way to them.

25294.label: Luke 6:32
25294.text: “And if YOU love those loving YOU, of what credit is it to YOU? For even the sinners love those loving them.

25295.label: Luke 6:33
25295.text: And if YOU do good to those doing good to YOU, really of what credit is it to YOU? Even the sinners do the same.

25296.label: Luke 6:34
25296.text: Also, if YOU lend [without interest] to those from whom YOU hope to receive, of what credit is it to YOU? Even sinners lend [without interest] to sinners that they may get back as much.

25297.label: Luke 6:35
25297.text: To the contrary, continue to love YOUR enemies and to do good and to lend [without interest], not hoping for anything back; and YOUR reward will be great, and YOU will be sons of the Most High, because he is kind toward the unthankful and wicked.

25298.label: Luke 6:36
25298.text: Continue becoming merciful, just as YOUR Father is merciful.

25299.label: Luke 6:37
25299.text: “Moreover, stop judging, and YOU will by no means be judged; and stop condemning, and YOU will by no means be condemned. Keep on releasing, and YOU will be released.

25300.label: Luke 6:38
25300.text: Practice giving, and people will give to YOU. They will pour into YOUR laps a fine measure, pressed down, shaken together and overflowing. For with the measure that YOU are measuring out, they will measure out to YOU in return.”

25301.label: Luke 6:39
25301.text: Then he also spoke an illustration to them: “A blind man cannot guide a blind man, can he? Both will tumble into a pit, will they not?

25302.label: Luke 6:40
25302.text: A pupil is not above his teacher, but everyone that is perfectly instructed will be like his teacher.

25303.label: Luke 6:41
25303.text: Why, then, do you look at the straw that is in your brother’s eye, but do not observe the rafter that is in your own eye?

25304.label: Luke 6:42
25304.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, allow me to extract the straw that is in your eye,’ while you yourself are not looking at the rafter in that eye of yours? Hypocrite! First extract the rafter from your own eye, and then you will see clearly how to extract the straw that is in your brother’s eye.

25305.label: Luke 6:43
25305.text: “For there is not a fine tree producing rotten fruit; again there is not a rotten tree producing fine fruit.

25306.label: Luke 6:44
25306.text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For example, people do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they cut grapes off a thornbush.

25307.label: Luke 6:45
25307.text: A good man brings forth good out of the good treasure of his heart, but a wicked man brings forth what is wicked out of his wicked [treasure]; for out of the heart’s abundance his mouth speaks.

25308.label: Luke 6:46
25308.text: “Why, then, do YOU call me ‘Lord! Lord!’ but do not do the things I say?

25309.label: Luke 6:47
25309.text: Everyone that comes to me and hears my words and does them, I will show YOU whom he is like:

25310.label: Luke 6:48
25310.text: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went down deep and laid a foundation upon the rock-mass. Consequently, when a flood arose, the river dashed against that house, but was not strong enough to shake it, because of its being well built.

25311.label: Luke 6:49
25311.text: On the other hand, he who hears and does not do, is like a man who built a house upon the ground without a foundation. Against it the river dashed, and immediately it collapsed, and the ruin of that house became great.”

25312.label: Luke 7:1
25312.text: When he had completed all his sayings in the hearing of the people, he entered into Ca·perʹna·um.

25313.label: Luke 7:2
25313.text: Now a certain army officer’s slave, who was dear to him, was ailing and was about to pass away.

25314.label: Luke 7:3
25314.text: When he heard about Jesus, he sent forth older men of the Jews to him to ask him to come and bring his slave safely through.

25315.label: Luke 7:4
25315.text: Then those that came up to Jesus began to entreat him earnestly, saying: “He is worthy of your conferring this upon him,

25316.label: Luke 7:5
25316.text: for he loves our nation and he himself built the synagogue for us.”

25317.label: Luke 7:6
25317.text: So Jesus started off with them. But when he was not far from the house, the army officer had already sent friends to say to him: “Sir, do not bother, for I am not fit to have you come in under my roof.

25318.label: Luke 7:7
25318.text: For that reason I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed.

25319.label: Luke 7:8
25319.text: For I too am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, ‘Be on your way!’ and he is on his way, and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this!’ and he does it.”

25320.label: Luke 7:9
25320.text: Well, when Jesus heard these things he marveled at him, and he turned to the crowd following him and said: “I tell YOU, Not even in Israel have I found so great a faith.”

25321.label: Luke 7:10
25321.text: And those that had been sent, on getting back to the house, found the slave in good health.

25322.label: Luke 7:11
25322.text: Closely following this he traveled to a city called Naʹin, and his disciples and a great crowd were traveling with him.

25323.label: Luke 7:12
25323.text: As he got near the gate of the city, why, look! there was a dead man being carried out, the only -begotten son of his mother. Besides, she was a widow. A considerable crowd from the city was also with her.

25324.label: Luke 7:13
25324.text: And when the Lord caught sight of her, he was moved with pity for her, and he said to her: “Stop weeping.”

25325.label: Luke 7:14
25325.text: With that he approached and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still, and he said: “Young man, I say to you, Get up!”

25326.label: Luke 7:15
25326.text: And the dead man sat up and started to speak, and he gave him to his mother.

25327.label: Luke 7:16
25327.text: Now fear seized them all, and they began to glorify God, saying: “A great prophet has been raised up among us,” and, “God has turned his attention to his people.”

25328.label: Luke 7:17
25328.text: And this news concerning him spread out into all Ju·deʹa and all the surrounding country.

25329.label: Luke 7:18
25329.text: Now John’s disciples reported to him about all these things.

25330.label: Luke 7:19
25330.text: So John summoned a certain two of his disciples and sent them to the Lord to say: “Are you the Coming One or are we to expect a different one?”

25331.label: Luke 7:20
25331.text: When they came up to him the men said: “John the Baptist dispatched us to you to say, ‘Are you the Coming One or are we to expect another?’”

25332.label: Luke 7:21
25332.text: In that hour he cured many of sicknesses and grievous diseases and wicked spirits, and granted many blind persons the favor of seeing.

25333.label: Luke 7:22
25333.text: Hence in answer he said to the [two]: “Go YOUR way, report to John what YOU saw and heard: the blind are receiving sight, the lame are walking, the lepers are being cleansed and the deaf are hearing, the dead are being raised up, the poor are being told the good news.

25334.label: Luke 7:23
25334.text: And happy is he who has not stumbled over me.”

25335.label: Luke 7:24
25335.text: When the messengers of John had gone away, he started to say to the crowds concerning John: “What did YOU go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed being tossed by the wind?

25336.label: Luke 7:25
25336.text: What, then, did YOU go out to see? A man dressed in soft outer garments? Why, those in splendid dress and existing in luxury are in royal houses.

25337.label: Luke 7:26
25337.text: Really, then, what did YOU go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell YOU, and far more than a prophet.

25338.label: Luke 7:27
25338.text: This is he concerning whom it is written, ‘Look! I am sending forth my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way ahead of you.’

25339.label: Luke 7:28
25339.text: I tell YOU, Among those born of women there is none greater than John; but a person that is a lesser one in the kingdom of God is greater than he is.”

25340.label: Luke 7:29
25340.text: (And all the people and the tax collectors, when they heard [this], declared God to be righteous, they having been baptized with the baptism of John.

25341.label: Luke 7:30
25341.text: But the Pharisees and those versed in the Law disregarded the counsel of God to them, they not having been baptized by him.)

25342.label: Luke 7:31
25342.text: “With whom, therefore, shall I compare the men of this generation, and whom are they like?

25343.label: Luke 7:32
25343.text: They are like young children sitting in a marketplace and crying out to one another, and who say, ‘We played the flute for YOU, but YOU did not dance; we wailed, but YOU did not weep.’

25344.label: Luke 7:33
25344.text: Correspondingly, John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, but YOU say, ‘He has a demon.’

25345.label: Luke 7:34
25345.text: The Son of man has come eating and drinking, but YOU say, ‘Look! A man gluttonous and given to drinking wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

25346.label: Luke 7:35
25346.text: All the same, wisdom is proved righteous by all its children.”

25347.label: Luke 7:36
25347.text: Now a certain one of the Pharisees kept asking him to dine with him. Accordingly he entered into the house of the Pharisee and reclined at the table.

25348.label: Luke 7:37
25348.text: And, look! a woman who was known in the city to be a sinner learned that he was reclining at a meal in the house of the Pharisee, and she brought an alabaster case of perfumed oil,

25349.label: Luke 7:38
25349.text: and, taking a position behind at his feet, she wept and started to wet his feet with her tears and she would wipe them off with the hair of her head. Also, she tenderly kissed his feet and greased them with the perfumed oil.

25350.label: Luke 7:39
25350.text: At the sight the Pharisee that invited him said within himself: “This man, if he were a prophet, would know who and what kind of woman it is that is touching him, that she is a sinner.”

25351.label: Luke 7:40
25351.text: But in reply Jesus said to him: “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said: “Teacher, say it!”

25352.label: Luke 7:41
25352.text: “Two men were debtors to a certain lender; the one was in debt for five hundred de·narʹi·i, but the other for fifty.

25353.label: Luke 7:42
25353.text: When they did not have anything with which to pay back, he freely forgave them both. Therefore, which of them will love him the more?”

25354.label: Luke 7:43
25354.text: In answer Simon said: “I suppose it is the one to whom he freely forgave the more.” He said to him: “You judged correctly.”

25355.label: Luke 7:44
25355.text: With that he turned to the woman and said to Simon: “Do you behold this woman? I entered into your house; you gave me no water for my feet. But this woman wet my feet with her tears and wiped them off with her hair.

25356.label: Luke 7:45
25356.text: You gave me no kiss; but this woman, from the hour that I came in, did not leave off tenderly kissing my feet.

25357.label: Luke 7:46
25357.text: You did not grease my head with oil; but this woman greased my feet with perfumed oil.

25358.label: Luke 7:47
25358.text: By virtue of this, I tell you, her sins, many though they are, are forgiven, because she loved much; but he who is forgiven little, loves little.”

25359.label: Luke 7:48
25359.text: Then he said to her: “Your sins are forgiven.”

25360.label: Luke 7:49
25360.text: At this those reclining at the table with him started to say within themselves: “Who is this man who even forgives sins?”

25361.label: Luke 7:50
25361.text: But he said to the woman: “Your faith has saved you; go your way in peace.”

25362.label: Luke 8:1
25362.text: Shortly afterwards he went journeying from city to city and from village to village, preaching and declaring the good news of the kingdom of God. And the twelve were with him,

25363.label: Luke 8:2
25363.text: and certain women that had been cured of wicked spirits and sicknesses, Mary the so-called Magʹda·lene, from whom seven demons had come out,

25364.label: Luke 8:3
25364.text: and Jo·anʹna the wife of Chuʹza, Herod’s man in charge, and Su·sanʹna and many other women, who were ministering to them from their belongings.

25365.label: Luke 8:4
25365.text: Now when a great crowd had collected together with those that went to him from city after city, he spoke by means of an illustration:

25366.label: Luke 8:5
25366.text: “A sower went out to sow his seed. Well, as he was sowing, some of it fell alongside the road and was trampled down, and the birds of heaven ate it up.

25367.label: Luke 8:6
25367.text: Some other landed upon the rock-mass, and, after sprouting, it dried up because of not having moisture.

25368.label: Luke 8:7
25368.text: Some other fell among the thorns, and the thorns that grew up with it choked it off.

25369.label: Luke 8:8
25369.text: Some other fell upon the good soil, and, after sprouting, it produced fruit a hundredfold.” As he told these things, he proceeded to call out: “Let him that has ears to listen, listen.”

25370.label: Luke 8:9
25370.text: But his disciples began to ask him what this illustration might mean.

25371.label: Luke 8:10
25371.text: He said: “To YOU it is granted to understand the sacred secrets of the kingdom of God, but for the rest it is in illustrations, in order that, though looking, they may look in vain and, though hearing, they may not get the meaning.

25372.label: Luke 8:11
25372.text: Now the illustration means this: The seed is the word of God.

25373.label: Luke 8:12
25373.text: Those alongside the road are the ones that have heard, then the Devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts in order that they may not believe and be saved.

25374.label: Luke 8:13
25374.text: Those upon the rock-mass are the ones who, when they hear it, receive the word with joy, but these have no root; they believe for a season, but in a season of testing they fall away.

25375.label: Luke 8:14
25375.text: As for that which fell among the thorns, these are the ones that have heard, but, by being carried away by anxieties and riches and pleasures of this life, they are completely choked and bring nothing to perfection.

25376.label: Luke 8:15
25376.text: As for that on the fine soil, these are the ones that, after hearing the word with a fine and good heart, retain it and bear fruit with endurance.

25377.label: Luke 8:16
25377.text: “No one, after lighting a lamp, covers it with a vessel or puts it underneath a bed, but he puts it on a lampstand, that those stepping in may behold the light.

25378.label: Luke 8:17
25378.text: For there is nothing hidden that will not become manifest, neither anything carefully concealed that will never become known and never come into the open.

25379.label: Luke 8:18
25379.text: Therefore, pay attention to how YOU listen; for whoever has, more will be given him, but whoever does not have, even what he imagines he has will be taken away from him.”

25380.label: Luke 8:19
25380.text: Now his mother and brothers came toward him, but they were unable to get to him because of the crowd.

25381.label: Luke 8:20
25381.text: However, it was reported to him: “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside wanting to see you.”

25382.label: Luke 8:21
25382.text: In reply he said to them: “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.”

25383.label: Luke 8:22
25383.text: In the course of one of the days he and his disciples got into a boat, and he said to them: “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So they set sail.

25384.label: Luke 8:23
25384.text: But as they were sailing he fell asleep. Now a violent windstorm descended upon the lake, and they began to fill up with [water] and to be in danger.

25385.label: Luke 8:24
25385.text: Finally they went to him and roused him, saying: “Instructor, Instructor, we are about to perish!” Rousing himself, he rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they subsided, and a calm set in.

25386.label: Luke 8:25
25386.text: Then he said to them: “Where is YOUR faith?” But struck with fear, they marveled, saying to one another: “Who really is this, for he orders even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

25387.label: Luke 8:26
25387.text: And they put in to shore in the country of the Gerʹa·senes, which is on the side opposite Galʹi·lee.

25388.label: Luke 8:27
25388.text: But as he got out onto land a certain man from the city who had demons met him. And for a considerable time he had not worn clothing, and he was staying, not at home, but among the tombs.

25389.label: Luke 8:28
25389.text: At the sight of Jesus he cried aloud and fell down before him, and with a loud voice he said: “What have I to do with you, Jesus Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”

25390.label: Luke 8:29
25390.text: (For he had been ordering the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For over a long time it had held him fast, and he was repeatedly bound with chains and fetters under guard, but he would burst the bonds and be driven by the demon into the lonely places.)

25391.label: Luke 8:30
25391.text: Jesus asked him: “What is your name?” He said: “Legion,” because many demons had entered into him.

25392.label: Luke 8:31
25392.text: And they kept entreating him not to order them to go away into the abyss.

25393.label: Luke 8:32
25393.text: Now a herd of a considerable number of swine was feeding there on the mountain; so they entreated him to permit them to enter into those. And he gave them permission.

25394.label: Luke 8:33
25394.text: Then the demons went out of the man and entered into the swine, and the herd rushed over the precipice into the lake and drowned.

25395.label: Luke 8:34
25395.text: But when the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it to the city and to the countryside.

25396.label: Luke 8:35
25396.text: Then people turned out to see what had happened, and they came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons came out, clothed and in his sound mind, sitting at the feet of Jesus; and they became fearful.

25397.label: Luke 8:36
25397.text: Those who had seen it reported to them how the demon-possessed man had been made well.

25398.label: Luke 8:37
25398.text: So all the multitude from the surrounding country of the Gerʹa·senes asked him to get away from them, because they were in the grip of great fear. Then he went aboard the boat and turned away.

25399.label: Luke 8:38
25399.text: However, the man from whom the demons had gone out kept begging to continue with him; but he dismissed the man, saying:

25400.label: Luke 8:39
25400.text: “Be on your way back home, and keep on relating what things God did for you.” Accordingly he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole city what things Jesus did for him.

25401.label: Luke 8:40
25401.text: When Jesus got back, the crowd received him kindly, for they were all expecting him.

25402.label: Luke 8:41
25402.text: But, look! a man named Jaʹi·rus came, and this man was a presiding officer of the synagogue. And he fell at the feet of Jesus and began to entreat him to enter into his house,

25403.label: Luke 8:42
25403.text: because he had an only-begotten daughter about twelve years old and she was dying. As he was going the crowds thronged him.

25404.label: Luke 8:43
25404.text: And a woman, subject to a flow of blood for twelve years, who had not been able to get a cure from anyone,

25405.label: Luke 8:44
25405.text: approached from behind and touched the fringe of his outer garment, and instantly her flow of blood stopped.

25406.label: Luke 8:45
25406.text: So Jesus said: “Who was it that touched me?” When they were all denying it, Peter said: “Instructor, the crowds are hemming you in and closely pressing you.”

25407.label: Luke 8:46
25407.text: Yet Jesus said: “Someone touched me, for I perceived that power went out of me.”

25408.label: Luke 8:47
25408.text: Seeing that she had not escaped notice, the woman came trembling and fell down before him and disclosed before all the people the cause for which she touched him and how she was healed instantly.

25409.label: Luke 8:48
25409.text: But he said to her: “Daughter, your faith has made you well; go your way in peace.”

25410.label: Luke 8:49
25410.text: While he was yet speaking, a certain representative of the presiding officer of the synagogue came, saying: “Your daughter has died; do not bother the teacher any longer.”

25411.label: Luke 8:50
25411.text: On hearing this, Jesus answered him: “Have no fear, only put forth faith, and she will be saved.”

25412.label: Luke 8:51
25412.text: When he reached the house he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter and John and James and the girl’s father and mother.

25413.label: Luke 8:52
25413.text: But people were all weeping and beating themselves in grief for her. So he said: “STOP weeping, for she did not die but is sleeping.”

25414.label: Luke 8:53
25414.text: At this they began to laugh at him scornfully, because they knew she had died.

25415.label: Luke 8:54
25415.text: But he took her by the hand and called, saying: “Girl, get up!”

25416.label: Luke 8:55
25416.text: And her spirit returned, and she rose instantly, and he ordered something to be given her to eat.

25417.label: Luke 8:56
25417.text: Well, her parents were beside themselves; but he instructed them to tell no one what had happened.

25418.label: Luke 9:1
25418.text: Then he called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all the demons and to cure sicknesses.

25419.label: Luke 9:2
25419.text: And so he sent them forth to preach the kingdom of God and to heal,

25420.label: Luke 9:3
25420.text: and he said to them: “Carry nothing for the trip, neither staff nor food pouch, nor bread nor silver money; neither have two undergarments.

25421.label: Luke 9:4
25421.text: But wherever YOU enter into a home, stay there and leave from there.

25422.label: Luke 9:5
25422.text: And wherever people do not receive YOU, on going out of that city shake the dust off YOUR feet for a witness against them.”

25423.label: Luke 9:6
25423.text: Then starting out they went through the territory from village to village, declaring the good news and performing cures everywhere.

25424.label: Luke 9:7
25424.text: Now Herod the district ruler heard of all the things happening, and he was in great perplexity because of its being said by some that John had been raised up from the dead,

25425.label: Luke 9:8
25425.text: but by others that E·liʹjah had appeared, but by still others that a certain one of the ancient prophets had risen.

25426.label: Luke 9:9
25426.text: Herod said: “John I beheaded. Who, then, is this about whom I am hearing such things?” So he was seeking to see him.

25427.label: Luke 9:10
25427.text: And when the apostles returned they recounted to him what things they had done. With that he took them along and withdrew to privacy into a city called Beth·saʹi·da.

25428.label: Luke 9:11
25428.text: But the crowds, getting to know it, followed him. And he received them kindly and began to speak to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those needing a cure.

25429.label: Luke 9:12
25429.text: Then the day started to decline. The twelve now came up and said to him: “Dismiss the crowd, that they may go into the villages and countryside round about and procure lodging and find provisions, because out here we are in a lonely place.”

25430.label: Luke 9:13
25430.text: But he said to them: “YOU give them something to eat.” They said: “We have nothing more than five loaves and two fishes, unless perhaps we ourselves go and buy foodstuffs for all these people.”

25431.label: Luke 9:14
25431.text: They were, in fact, about five thousand men. But he said to his disciples: “Have them recline as at meals, in groups of about fifty each.”

25432.label: Luke 9:15
25432.text: And they did so and had them all recline.

25433.label: Luke 9:16
25433.text: Then taking the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, blessed them and broke them up and began to give them to the disciples to set before the crowd.

25434.label: Luke 9:17
25434.text: So they all ate and were satisfied, and the surplus that they had was taken up, twelve baskets of fragments.

25435.label: Luke 9:18
25435.text: Later, while he was praying alone, the disciples came together to him, and he questioned them, saying: “Who are the crowds saying that I am?”

25436.label: Luke 9:19
25436.text: In reply they said: “John the Baptist; but others, E·liʹjah, and still others, that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”

25437.label: Luke 9:20
25437.text: Then he said to them: “YOU, though, who do YOU say I am?” Peter said in reply: “The Christ of God.”

25438.label: Luke 9:21
25438.text: Then in a stern talk to them he instructed them not to be telling this to anybody,

25439.label: Luke 9:22
25439.text: but said: “The Son of man must undergo many sufferings and be rejected by the older men and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised up.”

25440.label: Luke 9:23
25440.text: Then he went on to say to all: “If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself and pick up his torture stake day after day and follow me continually.

25441.label: Luke 9:24
25441.text: For whoever wants to save his soul will lose it; but whoever loses his soul for my sake is the one that will save it.

25442.label: Luke 9:25
25442.text: Really, what does a man benefit himself if he gains the whole world but loses his own self or suffers damage?

25443.label: Luke 9:26
25443.text: For whoever becomes ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of man will be ashamed of this one when he arrives in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.

25444.label: Luke 9:27
25444.text: But I tell YOU truthfully, There are some of those standing here that will not taste death at all until first they see the kingdom of God.”

25445.label: Luke 9:28
25445.text: In actual fact, about eight days after these words, he took Peter and John and James along and climbed up into the mountain to pray.

25446.label: Luke 9:29
25446.text: And as he was praying the appearance of his face became different and his apparel became glitteringly white.

25447.label: Luke 9:30
25447.text: Also, look! two men were conversing with him, who were Moses and E·liʹjah.

25448.label: Luke 9:31
25448.text: These appeared with glory and began talking about his departure that he was destined to fulfill at Jerusalem.

25449.label: Luke 9:32
25449.text: Now Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; but when they got fully awake they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

25450.label: Luke 9:33
25450.text: And as these were being separated from him, Peter said to Jesus: “Instructor, it is fine for us to be here, so let us erect three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for E·liʹjah,” he not realizing what he was saying.

25451.label: Luke 9:34
25451.text: But as he was saying these things a cloud formed and began to overshadow them. As they entered into the cloud, they became fearful.

25452.label: Luke 9:35
25452.text: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying: “This is my Son, the one that has been chosen. Listen to him.”

25453.label: Luke 9:36
25453.text: And as the voice occurred Jesus was found alone. But they kept quiet and did not report to anyone in those days any of the things they saw.

25454.label: Luke 9:37
25454.text: On the succeeding day, when they got down from the mountain, a great crowd met him.

25455.label: Luke 9:38
25455.text: And, look! a man cried out from the crowd, saying: “Teacher, I beg you to take a look at my son, because he is my only -begotten,

25456.label: Luke 9:39
25456.text: and, look! a spirit takes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it throws him into convulsions with foam, and it scarcely withdraws from him after bruising him.

25457.label: Luke 9:40
25457.text: And I begged your disciples to expel it, but they could not.”

25458.label: Luke 9:41
25458.text: In response Jesus said: “O faithless and twisted generation, how long must I continue with YOU and put up with YOU? Lead your son over here.”

25459.label: Luke 9:42
25459.text: But even as he was approaching, the demon dashed him to the ground and violently convulsed him. However, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and delivered him to his father.

25460.label: Luke 9:43
25460.text: Well, they all began to be astounded at the majestic power of God. Now as they were all marveling at all the things he was doing, he said to his disciples:

25461.label: Luke 9:44
25461.text: “Give lodgment to these words in YOUR ears, for the Son of man is destined to be delivered into the hands of men.”

25462.label: Luke 9:45
25462.text: But they continued without understanding of this saying. In fact, it was concealed from them that they might not see through it, and they were afraid to question him about this saying.

25463.label: Luke 9:46
25463.text: Then a reasoning entered among them as to who would be the greatest of them.

25464.label: Luke 9:47
25464.text: Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a young child, set it beside him

25465.label: Luke 9:48
25465.text: and said to them: “Whoever receives this young child on the basis of my name receives me [too], and whoever receives me receives him [also] that sent me forth. For he that conducts himself as a lesser one among all of YOU is the one that is great.”

25466.label: Luke 9:49
25466.text: In response John said: “Instructor, we saw a certain man expelling demons by the use of your name and we tried to prevent him, because he is not following with us.”

25467.label: Luke 9:50
25467.text: But Jesus said to him: “Do not YOU men try to prevent [him], for he that is not against YOU is for YOU.”

25468.label: Luke 9:51
25468.text: As the days were now coming to the full for him to be taken up, he firmly set his face to go to Jerusalem.

25469.label: Luke 9:52
25469.text: So he sent forth messengers in advance of him. And they went their way and entered into a village of Sa·marʹi·tans, to make preparation for him;

25470.label: Luke 9:53
25470.text: but they did not receive him, because his face was set for going to Jerusalem.

25471.label: Luke 9:54
25471.text: When the disciples James and John saw this they said: “Lord, do you want us to tell fire to come down from heaven and annihilate them?”

25472.label: Luke 9:55
25472.text: But he turned and rebuked them.

25473.label: Luke 9:56
25473.text: So they went to a different village.

25474.label: Luke 9:57
25474.text: Now as they were going on the road, someone said to him: “I will follow you to wherever you may depart.”

25475.label: Luke 9:58
25475.text: And Jesus said to him: “Foxes have dens and birds of heaven have roosts, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay down his head.”

25476.label: Luke 9:59
25476.text: Then he said to another: “Be my follower.” The man said: “Permit me first to leave and bury my father.”

25477.label: Luke 9:60
25477.text: But he said to him: “Let the dead bury their dead, but you go away and declare abroad the kingdom of God.”

25478.label: Luke 9:61
25478.text: And still another said: “I will follow you, Lord; but first permit me to say good-bye to those in my household.”

25479.label: Luke 9:62
25479.text: Jesus said to him: “No man that has put his hand to a plow and looks at the things behind is well fitted for the kingdom of God.”

25480.label: Luke 10:1
25480.text: After these things the Lord designated seventy others and sent them forth by twos in advance of him into every city and place to which he himself was going to come.

25481.label: Luke 10:2
25481.text: Then he began to say to them: “The harvest, indeed, is great, but the workers are few. Therefore beg the Master of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.

25482.label: Luke 10:3
25482.text: Go forth. Look! I am sending YOU forth as lambs in among wolves.

25483.label: Luke 10:4
25483.text: Do not carry a purse, nor a food pouch, nor sandals, and do not embrace anybody in greeting along the road.

25484.label: Luke 10:5
25484.text: Wherever YOU enter into a house say first, ‘May this house have peace.’

25485.label: Luke 10:6
25485.text: And if a friend of peace is there, YOUR peace will rest upon him. But if there is not, it will turn back to YOU.

25486.label: Luke 10:7
25486.text: So stay in that house, eating and drinking the things they provide, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not be transferring from house to house.

25487.label: Luke 10:8
25487.text: “Also, wherever YOU enter into a city and they receive YOU, eat the things set before YOU,

25488.label: Luke 10:9
25488.text: and cure the sick ones in it, and go on telling them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to YOU.’

25489.label: Luke 10:10
25489.text: But wherever YOU enter into a city and they do not receive YOU, go out into its broad ways and say,

25490.label: Luke 10:11
25490.text: ‘Even the dust that got stuck to our feet from YOUR city we wipe off against YOU. Nevertheless, keep this in mind, that the kingdom of God has come near.’

25491.label: Luke 10:12
25491.text: I tell YOU that it will be more endurable for Sodʹom in that day than for that city.

25492.label: Luke 10:13
25492.text: “Woe to you, Cho·raʹzin! Woe to you, Beth·saʹi·da! because if the powerful works that have taken place in YOU had taken place in Tyre and Siʹdon, they would long ago have repented sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

25493.label: Luke 10:14
25493.text: Consequently it will be more endurable for Tyre and Siʹdon in the judgment than for YOU.

25494.label: Luke 10:15
25494.text: And you, Ca·perʹna·um, will you perhaps be exalted to heaven? Down to Haʹdes you will come!

25495.label: Luke 10:16
25495.text: “He that listens to YOU listens to me [too]. And he that disregards YOU disregards me [too]. Moreover, he that disregards me disregards [also] him that sent me forth.”

25496.label: Luke 10:17
25496.text: Then the seventy returned with joy, saying: “Lord, even the demons are made subject to us by the use of your name.”

25497.label: Luke 10:18
25497.text: At that he said to them: “I began to behold Satan already fallen like lightning from heaven.

25498.label: Luke 10:19
25498.text: Look! I have given YOU the authority to trample underfoot serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will by any means do YOU hurt.

25499.label: Luke 10:20
25499.text: Nevertheless, do not rejoice over this, that the spirits are made subject to YOU, but rejoice because YOUR names have been inscribed in the heavens.”

25500.label: Luke 10:21
25500.text: In that very hour he became overjoyed in the holy spirit and said: “I publicly praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have carefully hidden these things from wise and intellectual ones, and have revealed them to babes. Yes, O Father, because to do thus came to be the way approved by you.

25501.label: Luke 10:22
25501.text: All things have been delivered to me by my Father, and who the Son is no one knows but the Father; and who the Father is, no one [knows] but the Son, and he to whom the Son is willing to reveal him.”

25502.label: Luke 10:23
25502.text: With that he turned to the disciples by themselves and said: “Happy are the eyes that behold the things YOU are beholding.

25503.label: Luke 10:24
25503.text: For I say to YOU, Many prophets and kings desired to see the things YOU are beholding but did not see them, and to hear the things YOU are hearing but did not hear them.”

25504.label: Luke 10:25
25504.text: Now, look! a certain man versed in the Law rose up, to test him out, and said: “Teacher, by doing what shall I inherit everlasting life?”

25505.label: Luke 10:26
