25505.text: He said to him: “What is written in the Law? How do you read?”

25506.label: Luke 10:27
25506.text: In answer he said: “‘You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole strength and with your whole mind,’ and, ‘your neighbor as yourself.’”

25507.label: Luke 10:28
25507.text: He said to him: “You answered correctly; ‘keep on doing this and you will get life.’”

25508.label: Luke 10:29
25508.text: But, wanting to prove himself righteous, the man said to Jesus: “Who really is my neighbor?”

25509.label: Luke 10:30
25509.text: In reply Jesus said: “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jerʹi·cho and fell among robbers, who both stripped him and inflicted blows, and went off, leaving him half-dead.

25510.label: Luke 10:31
25510.text: Now, by coincidence, a certain priest was going down over that road, but, when he saw him, he went by on the opposite side.

25511.label: Luke 10:32
25511.text: Likewise, a Levite also, when he got down to the place and saw him, went by on the opposite side.

25512.label: Luke 10:33
25512.text: But a certain Sa·marʹi·tan traveling the road came upon him and, at seeing him, he was moved with pity.

25513.label: Luke 10:34
25513.text: So he approached him and bound up his wounds, pouring oil and wine upon them. Then he mounted him upon his own beast and brought him to an inn and took care of him.

25514.label: Luke 10:35
25514.text: And the next day he took out two de·narʹi·i, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Take care of him, and whatever you spend besides this, I will repay you when I come back here.’

25515.label: Luke 10:36
25515.text: Who of these three seems to you to have made himself neighbor to the man that fell among the robbers?”

25516.label: Luke 10:37
25516.text: He said: “The one that acted mercifully toward him.” Jesus then said to him: “Go your way and be doing the same yourself.”

25517.label: Luke 10:38
25517.text: Now as they were going their way he entered into a certain village. Here a certain woman named Martha received him as guest into the house.

25518.label: Luke 10:39
25518.text: This woman also had a sister called Mary, who, however, sat down at the feet of the Lord and kept listening to his word.

25519.label: Luke 10:40
25519.text: Martha, on the other hand, was distracted with attending to many duties. So, she came near and said: “Lord, does it not matter to you that my sister has left me alone to attend to things? Tell her, therefore, to join in helping me.”

25520.label: Luke 10:41
25520.text: In answer the Lord said to her: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and disturbed about many things.

25521.label: Luke 10:42
25521.text: A few things, though, are needed, or just one. For her part, Mary chose the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”

25522.label: Luke 11:1
25522.text: Now on the occasion of his being in a certain place praying, when he stopped, a certain one of his disciples said to him: “Lord, teach us how to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”

25523.label: Luke 11:2
25523.text: Then he said to them: “Whenever YOU pray, say, ‘Father, let your name be sanctified. Let your kingdom come.

25524.label: Luke 11:3
25524.text: Give us our bread for the day according to the day’s requirement.

25525.label: Luke 11:4
25525.text: And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone that is in debt to us; and do not bring us into temptation.’”

25526.label: Luke 11:5
25526.text: Further, he said to them: “Who of YOU will have a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, loan me three loaves,

25527.label: Luke 11:6
25527.text: because a friend of mine has just come to me on a journey and I have nothing to set before him’?

25528.label: Luke 11:7
25528.text: And that one from inside says in reply, ‘Quit making me trouble. The door is already locked, and my young children are with me in bed; I cannot rise up and give you anything.’

25529.label: Luke 11:8
25529.text: I tell YOU, Although he will not rise up and give him anything because of being his friend, certainly because of his bold persistence he will get up and give him what things he needs.

25530.label: Luke 11:9
25530.text: Accordingly I say to YOU, Keep on asking, and it will be given YOU; keep on seeking, and YOU will find; keep on knocking, and it will be opened to YOU.

25531.label: Luke 11:10
25531.text: For everyone asking receives, and everyone seeking finds, and to everyone knocking it will be opened.

25532.label: Luke 11:11
25532.text: Indeed, which father is there among YOU who, if his son asks for a fish, will perhaps hand him a serpent instead of a fish?

25533.label: Luke 11:12
25533.text: Or if he also asks for an egg, will hand him a scorpion?

25534.label: Luke 11:13
25534.text: Therefore, if YOU, although being wicked, know how to give good gifts to YOUR children, how much more so will the Father in heaven give holy spirit to those asking him!”

25535.label: Luke 11:14
25535.text: Later he was expelling a dumb demon. After the demon came out, the dumb man spoke. And the crowds marveled.

25536.label: Luke 11:15
25536.text: But certain ones of them said: “He expels the demons by means of Be·elʹze·bub the ruler of the demons.”

25537.label: Luke 11:16
25537.text: However, others, to tempt him, began seeking a sign out of heaven from him.

25538.label: Luke 11:17
25538.text: Knowing their imaginations he said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself comes to desolation, and a house [divided] against itself falls.

25539.label: Luke 11:18
25539.text: So if Satan is also divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because YOU say I expel the demons by means of Be·elʹze·bub.

25540.label: Luke 11:19
25540.text: If it is by means of Be·elʹze·bub I expel the demons, by whom do YOUR sons expel them? Because of this they will be judges of YOU.

25541.label: Luke 11:20
25541.text: But if it is by means of God’s finger I expel the demons, the kingdom of God has really overtaken YOU.

25542.label: Luke 11:21
25542.text: When a strong man, well armed, guards his palace, his belongings continue in peace.

25543.label: Luke 11:22
25543.text: But when someone stronger than he is comes against him and conquers him, he takes away his full armament in which he was trusting, and he divides out the things he despoiled him of.

25544.label: Luke 11:23
25544.text: He that is not on my side is against me, and he that does not gather with me scatters.

25545.label: Luke 11:24
25545.text: “When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through parched places in search of a resting-place, and, after finding none, it says, ‘I will return to my house out of which I moved.’

25546.label: Luke 11:25
25546.text: And on arriving it finds it swept clean and adorned.

25547.label: Luke 11:26
25547.text: Then it goes its way and takes along seven different spirits more wicked than itself, and, after getting inside, they dwell there; and the final circumstances of that man become worse than the first.”

25548.label: Luke 11:27
25548.text: Now as he was saying these things a certain woman out of the crowd raised her voice and said to him: “Happy is the womb that carried you and the breasts that you sucked!”

25549.label: Luke 11:28
25549.text: But he said: “No, rather, Happy are those hearing the word of God and keeping it!”

25550.label: Luke 11:29
25550.text: When the crowds were massing together, he started to say: “This generation is a wicked generation; it looks for a sign. But no sign will be given it except the sign of Joʹnah.

25551.label: Luke 11:30
25551.text: For just as Joʹnah became a sign to the Ninʹe·vites, in the same way will the Son of man be also to this generation.

25552.label: Luke 11:31
25552.text: The queen of the south will be raised up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them; because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solʹo·mon, but, look! something more than Solʹo·mon is here.

25553.label: Luke 11:32
25553.text: The men of Ninʹe·veh will rise in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it; because they repented at what Joʹnah preached; but, look! something more than Joʹnah is here.

25554.label: Luke 11:33
25554.text: After lighting a lamp, a person puts it, not in a vault nor under a measuring basket, but upon the lampstand, that those stepping in may behold the light.

25555.label: Luke 11:34
25555.text: The lamp of the body is your eye. When your eye is simple, your whole body is also bright; but when it is wicked, your body is also dark.

25556.label: Luke 11:35
25556.text: Be alert, therefore. Perhaps the light that is in you is darkness.

25557.label: Luke 11:36
25557.text: Therefore, if your whole body is bright with no part at all dark, it will all be as bright as when a lamp gives you light by its rays.”

25558.label: Luke 11:37
25558.text: When he had spoken this, a Pharisee requested him to dine with him. So he went in and reclined at the table.

25559.label: Luke 11:38
25559.text: However, the Pharisee was surprised at seeing that he did not first wash before the dinner.

25560.label: Luke 11:39
25560.text: But the Lord said to him: “Now YOU Pharisees, YOU cleanse the outside of the cup and dish, but the inside of YOU is full of plunder and wickedness.

25561.label: Luke 11:40
25561.text: Unreasonable persons! He that made the outside made also the inside, did he not?

25562.label: Luke 11:41
25562.text: Nevertheless, give as gifts of mercy the things that are inside, and, look! all [other] things are clean about YOU.

25563.label: Luke 11:42
25563.text: But woe to YOU Pharisees, because YOU give the tenth of the mint and the rue and of every [other] vegetable, but YOU pass by the justice and the love of God! These things YOU were under obligation to do, but those other things not to omit.

25564.label: Luke 11:43
25564.text: Woe to YOU Pharisees, because YOU love the front seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces!

25565.label: Luke 11:44
25565.text: Woe to YOU, because YOU are as those memorial tombs which are not in evidence, so that men walk upon them and do not know [it]!”

25566.label: Luke 11:45
25566.text: In answer a certain one of those versed in the Law said to him: “Teacher, in saying these things you also insult us.”

25567.label: Luke 11:46
25567.text: Then he said: “Woe also to YOU who are versed in the Law, because YOU load men with loads hard to be borne, but YOU yourselves do not touch the loads with one of YOUR fingers!

25568.label: Luke 11:47
25568.text: “Woe to YOU, because YOU build the memorial tombs of the prophets, but YOUR forefathers killed them!

25569.label: Luke 11:48
25569.text: Certainly YOU are witnesses of the deeds of YOUR forefathers and yet YOU give consent to them, because these killed the prophets but YOU are building [their tombs].

25570.label: Luke 11:49
25570.text: On this account the wisdom of God also said, ‘I will send forth to them prophets and apostles, and they will kill and persecute some of them,

25571.label: Luke 11:50
25571.text: so that the blood of all the prophets spilled from the founding of the world may be required from this generation,

25572.label: Luke 11:51
25572.text: from the blood of Abel down to the blood of Zech·a·riʹah, who was slain between the altar and the house.’ Yes, I tell YOU, it will be required from this generation.

25573.label: Luke 11:52
25573.text: “Woe to YOU who are versed in the Law, because YOU took away the key of knowledge; YOU yourselves did not go in, and those going in YOU hindered!”

25574.label: Luke 11:53
25574.text: So when he went out from there the scribes and the Pharisees started in to press upon him terribly and to ply him with questions about further things,

25575.label: Luke 11:54
25575.text: lying in wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth.

25576.label: Luke 12:1
25576.text: In the meantime, when the crowd had gathered together in so many thousands that they were stepping upon one another, he started out by saying first to his disciples: “Watch out for the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

25577.label: Luke 12:2
25577.text: But there is nothing carefully concealed that will not be revealed, and secret that will not become known.

25578.label: Luke 12:3
25578.text: Wherefore what things YOU say in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what YOU whisper in private rooms will be preached from the housetops.

25579.label: Luke 12:4
25579.text: Moreover, I say to YOU, my friends, Do not fear those who kill the body and after this are not able to do anything more.

25580.label: Luke 12:5
25580.text: But I will indicate to YOU whom to fear: Fear him who after killing has authority to throw into Ge·henʹna. Yes, I tell YOU, fear this One.

25581.label: Luke 12:6
25581.text: Five sparrows sell for two coins of small value, do they not? Yet not one of them goes forgotten before God.

25582.label: Luke 12:7
25582.text: But even the hairs of YOUR heads are all numbered. Have no fear; YOU are worth more than many sparrows.

25583.label: Luke 12:8
25583.text: “I say, then, to YOU, Everyone that confesses union with me before men, the Son of man will also confess union with him before the angels of God.

25584.label: Luke 12:9
25584.text: But he that disowns me before men will be disowned before the angels of God.

25585.label: Luke 12:10
25585.text: And everyone that says a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; but he that blasphemes against the holy spirit will not be forgiven it.

25586.label: Luke 12:11
25586.text: But when they bring YOU in before public assemblies and government officials and authorities, do not become anxious about how or what YOU will speak in defense or what YOU will say;

25587.label: Luke 12:12
25587.text: for the holy spirit will teach YOU in that very hour the things YOU ought to say.”

25588.label: Luke 12:13
25588.text: Then a certain one of the crowd said to him: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

25589.label: Luke 12:14
25589.text: He said to him: “Man, who appointed me judge or apportioner over YOU persons?”

25590.label: Luke 12:15
25590.text: Then he said to them: “Keep YOUR eyes open and guard against every sort of covetousness, because even when a person has an abundance his life does not result from the things he possesses.”

25591.label: Luke 12:16
25591.text: With that he spoke an illustration to them, saying: “The land of a certain rich man produced well.

25592.label: Luke 12:17
25592.text: Consequently he began reasoning within himself, saying, ‘What shall I do, now that I have nowhere to gather my crops?’

25593.label: Luke 12:18
25593.text: So he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my storehouses and build bigger ones, and there I will gather all my grain and all my good things;

25594.label: Luke 12:19
25594.text: and I will say to my soul: “Soul, you have many good things laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.”’

25595.label: Luke 12:20
25595.text: But God said to him, ‘Unreasonable one, this night they are demanding your soul from you. Who, then, is to have the things you stored up?’

25596.label: Luke 12:21
25596.text: So it goes with the man that lays up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”

25597.label: Luke 12:22
25597.text: Then he said to his disciples: “On this account I say to YOU, Quit being anxious about YOUR souls as to what YOU will eat or about YOUR bodies as to what YOU will wear.

25598.label: Luke 12:23
25598.text: For the soul is worth more than food and the body than clothing.

25599.label: Luke 12:24
25599.text: Mark well that the ravens neither sow seed nor reap, and they have neither barn nor storehouse, and yet God feeds them. Of how much more worth are YOU than birds?

25600.label: Luke 12:25
25600.text: Who of YOU by being anxious can add a cubit to his life span?

25601.label: Luke 12:26
25601.text: If, therefore, YOU cannot do the least thing, why be anxious about the remaining things?

25602.label: Luke 12:27
25602.text: Mark well how the lilies grow; they neither toil nor spin; but I tell YOU, Not even Solʹo·mon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these.

25603.label: Luke 12:28
25603.text: If, now, God thus clothes the vegetation in the field that today exists and tomorrow is cast into an oven, how much rather will he clothe YOU, YOU with little faith!

25604.label: Luke 12:29
25604.text: So quit seeking what YOU might eat and what YOU might drink, and quit being in anxious suspense;

25605.label: Luke 12:30
25605.text: for all these are the things the nations of the world are eagerly pursuing, but YOUR Father knows YOU need these things.

25606.label: Luke 12:31
25606.text: Nevertheless, seek continually his kingdom, and these things will be added to YOU.

25607.label: Luke 12:32
25607.text: “Have no fear, little flock, because YOUR Father has approved of giving YOU the kingdom.

25608.label: Luke 12:33
25608.text: Sell the things belonging to YOU and give gifts of mercy. Make purses for yourselves that do not wear out, a never-failing treasure in the heavens, where a thief does not get near nor moth consumes.

25609.label: Luke 12:34
25609.text: For where YOUR treasure is, there YOUR hearts will be also.

25610.label: Luke 12:35
25610.text: “Let YOUR loins be girded and YOUR lamps be burning,

25611.label: Luke 12:36
25611.text: and YOU yourselves be like men waiting for their master when he returns from the marriage, so that at his arriving and knocking they may at once open to him.

25612.label: Luke 12:37
25612.text: Happy are those slaves whom the master on arriving finds watching! Truly I say to YOU, He will gird himself and make them recline at the table and will come alongside and minister to them.

25613.label: Luke 12:38
25613.text: And if he arrives in the second watch, even if in the third, and finds them thus, happy are they!

25614.label: Luke 12:39
25614.text: But know this, that if the householder had known at what hour the thief would come, he would have kept watching and not have let his house be broken into.

25615.label: Luke 12:40
25615.text: YOU also, keep ready, because at an hour that YOU do not think likely the Son of man is coming.”

25616.label: Luke 12:41
25616.text: Then Peter said: “Lord, are you saying this illustration to us or also to all?”

25617.label: Luke 12:42
25617.text: And the Lord said: “Who really is the faithful steward, the discreet one, whom his master will appoint over his body of attendants to keep giving them their measure of food supplies at the proper time?

25618.label: Luke 12:43
25618.text: Happy is that slave, if his master on arriving finds him doing so!

25619.label: Luke 12:44
25619.text: I tell YOU truthfully, He will appoint him over all his belongings.

25620.label: Luke 12:45
25620.text: But if ever that slave should say in his heart, ‘My master delays coming,’ and should start to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,

25621.label: Luke 12:46
25621.text: the master of that slave will come on a day that he is not expecting [him] and in an hour that he does not know, and he will punish him with the greatest severity and assign him a part with the unfaithful ones.

25622.label: Luke 12:47
25622.text: Then that slave that understood the will of his master but did not get ready or do in line with his will will be beaten with many strokes.

25623.label: Luke 12:48
25623.text: But the one that did not understand and so did things deserving of strokes will be beaten with few. Indeed, everyone to whom much was given, much will be demanded of him; and the one whom people put in charge of much, they will demand more than usual of him.

25624.label: Luke 12:49
25624.text: “I came to start a fire on the earth, and what more is there for me to wish if it has already been lighted?

25625.label: Luke 12:50
25625.text: Indeed, I have a baptism with which to be baptized, and how I am being distressed until it is finished!

25626.label: Luke 12:51
25626.text: Do YOU imagine I came to give peace on the earth? No, indeed, I tell YOU, but rather division.

25627.label: Luke 12:52
25627.text: For from now on there will be five in one house divided, three against two and two against three.

25628.label: Luke 12:53
25628.text: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against [her] mother, mother-in-law against [her] daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against [her] mother-in-law.”

25629.label: Luke 12:54
25629.text: Then he went on to say also to the crowds: “When YOU see a cloud rising in western parts, at once YOU say, ‘A storm is coming,’ and it turns out so.

25630.label: Luke 12:55
25630.text: And when YOU see that a south wind is blowing, YOU say, ‘There will be a heat wave,’ and it occurs.

25631.label: Luke 12:56
25631.text: Hypocrites, YOU know how to examine the outward appearance of earth and sky, but how is it YOU do not know how to examine this particular time?

25632.label: Luke 12:57
25632.text: Why do YOU not judge also for yourselves what is righteous?

25633.label: Luke 12:58
25633.text: For example, when you are going with your adversary at law to a ruler, get to work, while on the way, to rid yourself of the dispute with him, that he may never hale you before the judge, and the judge deliver you to the court officer, and the court officer throw you into prison.

25634.label: Luke 12:59
25634.text: I tell you, You will certainly not get out from there until you pay over the last small coin of very little value.”

25635.label: Luke 13:1
25635.text: At that very season there were certain ones present that reported to him about the Gal·i·leʹans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

25636.label: Luke 13:2
25636.text: So in reply he said to them: “Do YOU imagine that these Gal·i·leʹans were proved worse sinners than all other Gal·i·leʹans because they have suffered these things?

25637.label: Luke 13:3
25637.text: No, indeed, I tell YOU; but, unless YOU repent, YOU will all likewise be destroyed.

25638.label: Luke 13:4
25638.text: Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Si·loʹam fell, thereby killing them, do YOU imagine that they were proved greater debtors than all other men inhabiting Jerusalem?

25639.label: Luke 13:5
25639.text: No, indeed, I tell YOU; but, unless YOU repent, YOU will all be destroyed in the same way.”

25640.label: Luke 13:6
25640.text: Then he went on to tell this illustration: “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it, but found none.

25641.label: Luke 13:7
25641.text: Then he said to the vinedresser, ‘Here it is three years that I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, but have found none. Cut it down! Why really should it keep the ground useless?’

25642.label: Luke 13:8
25642.text: In reply he said to him, ‘Master, let it alone also this year, until I dig around it and put on manure;

25643.label: Luke 13:9
25643.text: and if then it produces fruit in the future, [well and good]; but if not, you shall cut it down.’”

25644.label: Luke 13:10
25644.text: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

25645.label: Luke 13:11
25645.text: And, look! a woman with a spirit of weakness for eighteen years, and she was bent double and was unable to raise herself up at all.

25646.label: Luke 13:12
25646.text: When he saw her, Jesus addressed her and said to her: “Woman, you are released from your weakness.”

25647.label: Luke 13:13
25647.text: And he laid his hands on her; and instantly she straightened up, and began to glorify God.

25648.label: Luke 13:14
25648.text: But in response the presiding officer of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus did the cure on the sabbath, began to say to the crowd: “There are six days on which work ought to be done; on them, therefore, come and be cured, and not on the sabbath day.”

25649.label: Luke 13:15
25649.text: However, the Lord answered him and said: “Hypocrites, does not each one of YOU on the sabbath untie his bull or his ass from the stall and lead it away to give it drink?

25650.label: Luke 13:16
25650.text: Was it not due, then, for this woman who is a daughter of Abraham, and whom Satan held bound, look! eighteen years, to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?”

25651.label: Luke 13:17
25651.text: Well, when he said these things, all his opposers began to feel shame; but all the crowd began to rejoice at all the glorious things done by him.

25652.label: Luke 13:18
25652.text: Therefore he went on to say: “What is the kingdom of God like, and with what shall I compare it?

25653.label: Luke 13:19
25653.text: It is like a mustard grain that a man took and put in his garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of heaven took up lodging in its branches.”

25654.label: Luke 13:20
25654.text: And again he said: “With what shall I compare the kingdom of God?

25655.label: Luke 13:21
25655.text: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three large measures of flour until the whole mass was fermented.”

25656.label: Luke 13:22
25656.text: And he journeyed through from city to city and from village to village, teaching and continuing on his journey to Jerusalem.

25657.label: Luke 13:23
25657.text: Now a certain man said to him: “Lord, are those who are being saved few?” He said to them:

25658.label: Luke 13:24
25658.text: “Exert yourselves vigorously to get in through the narrow door, because many, I tell YOU, will seek to get in but will not be able,

25659.label: Luke 13:25
25659.text: when once the householder has got up and locked the door, and YOU start to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Sir, open to us.’ But in answer he will say to YOU, ‘I do not know where YOU are from.’

25660.label: Luke 13:26
25660.text: Then YOU will start saying, ‘We ate and drank in front of you, and you taught in our broad ways.’

25661.label: Luke 13:27
25661.text: But he will speak and say to YOU, ‘I do not know where YOU are from. Get away from me, all YOU workers of unrighteousness!’

25662.label: Luke 13:28
25662.text: There is where [YOUR] weeping and the gnashing of [YOUR] teeth will be, when YOU see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown outside.

25663.label: Luke 13:29
25663.text: Furthermore, people will come from eastern parts and western, and from north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.

25664.label: Luke 13:30
25664.text: And, look! there are those last who will be first, and there are those first who will be last.”

25665.label: Luke 13:31
25665.text: In that very hour certain Pharisees came up, saying to him: “Get out and be on your way from here, because Herod wants to kill you.”

25666.label: Luke 13:32
25666.text: And he said to them: “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look! I am casting out demons and accomplishing healing today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be finished.’

25667.label: Luke 13:33
25667.text: Nevertheless, I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the following day, because it is not admissible for a prophet to be destroyed outside of Jerusalem.

25668.label: Luke 13:34
25668.text: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the killer of the prophets and stoner of those sent forth to her—how often I wanted to gather your children together in the manner that a hen gathers her brood of chicks under her wings, but YOU people did not want [it]!

25669.label: Luke 13:35
25669.text: Look! YOUR house is abandoned to YOU. I tell YOU, YOU will by no means see me until YOU say, ‘Blessed is he that comes in Jehovah’s name.’”

25670.label: Luke 14:1
25670.text: And on an occasion when he went into the house of a certain one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the sabbath to eat a meal, they were closely watching him.

25671.label: Luke 14:2
25671.text: And, look! there was before him a certain man who had dropsy.

25672.label: Luke 14:3
25672.text: So in response Jesus spoke to those versed in the Law and to the Pharisees, saying: “Is it lawful on the sabbath to cure or not?”

25673.label: Luke 14:4
25673.text: But they kept silent. With that he took hold of [the man], healed him and sent [him] away.

25674.label: Luke 14:5
25674.text: And he said to them: “Who of YOU, if his son or bull falls into a well, will not immediately pull him out on the sabbath day?”

25675.label: Luke 14:6
25675.text: And they were not able to answer back on these things.

25676.label: Luke 14:7
25676.text: He then went on to tell the invited men an illustration, as he marked how they were choosing the most prominent places for themselves, saying to them:

25677.label: Luke 14:8
25677.text: “When you are invited by someone to a marriage feast, do not lie down in the most prominent place. Perhaps someone more distinguished than you may at the time have been invited by him,

25678.label: Luke 14:9
25678.text: and he that invited you and him will come and say to you, ‘Let this man have the place.’ And then you will start off with shame to occupy the lowest place.

25679.label: Luke 14:10
25679.text: But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, that when the man that has invited you comes he will say to you, ‘Friend, go on up higher.’ Then you will have honor in front of all your fellow guests.

25680.label: Luke 14:11
25680.text: For everyone that exalts himself will be humbled and he that humbles himself will be exalted.”

25681.label: Luke 14:12
25681.text: Next he proceeded to say also to the man that invited him: “When you spread a dinner or evening meal, do not call your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors. Perhaps sometime they might also invite you in return and it would become a repayment to you.

25682.label: Luke 14:13
25682.text: But when you spread a feast, invite poor people, crippled, lame, blind;

25683.label: Luke 14:14
25683.text: and you will be happy, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous ones.”

25684.label: Luke 14:15
25684.text: On hearing these things a certain one of the fellow guests said to him: “Happy is he who eats bread in the kingdom of God.”

25685.label: Luke 14:16
25685.text: [Jesus] said to him: “A certain man was spreading a grand evening meal, and he invited many.

25686.label: Luke 14:17
25686.text: And he sent his slave out at the hour of the evening meal to say to the invited ones, ‘Come, because things are now ready.’

25687.label: Luke 14:18
25687.text: But they all in common started to beg off. The first said to him, ‘I bought a field and need to go out and see it; I ask you, Have me excused.’

25688.label: Luke 14:19
25688.text: And another said, ‘I bought five yoke of cattle and am going to examine them; I ask you, Have me excused.’

25689.label: Luke 14:20
25689.text: Still another said, ‘I just married a wife and for this reason I cannot come.’

25690.label: Luke 14:21
25690.text: So the slave came up and reported these things to his master. Then the householder became wrathful and said to his slave, ‘Go out quickly into the broad ways and the lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame.’

25691.label: Luke 14:22
25691.text: In time the slave said, ‘Master, what you ordered has been done, and yet there is room.’

25692.label: Luke 14:23
25692.text: And the master said to the slave, ‘Go out into the roads and the fenced-in places, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

25693.label: Luke 14:24
25693.text: For I say to YOU people, None of those men that were invited shall have a taste of my evening meal.’”

25694.label: Luke 14:25
25694.text: Now great crowds were traveling with him, and he turned and said to them:

25695.label: Luke 14:26
25695.text: “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own soul, he cannot be my disciple.

25696.label: Luke 14:27
25696.text: Whoever is not carrying his torture stake and coming after me cannot be my disciple.

25697.label: Luke 14:28
25697.text: For example, who of YOU that wants to build a tower does not first sit down and calculate the expense, to see if he has enough to complete it?

25698.label: Luke 14:29
25698.text: Otherwise, he might lay its foundation but not be able to finish it, and all the onlookers might start to ridicule him,

25699.label: Luke 14:30
25699.text: saying, ‘This man started to build but was not able to finish.’

25700.label: Luke 14:31
25700.text: Or what king, marching to meet another king in war, does not first sit down and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand troops to cope with the one that comes against him with twenty thousand?

25701.label: Luke 14:32
25701.text: If, in fact, he cannot do so, then while that one is yet far away he sends out a body of ambassadors and sues for peace.

25702.label: Luke 14:33
25702.text: Thus, you may be sure, none of YOU that does not say good-bye to all his belongings can be my disciple.

25703.label: Luke 14:34
25703.text: “Salt, to be sure, is fine. But if even the salt loses its strength, with what will it be seasoned?

25704.label: Luke 14:35
25704.text: It is suitable neither for soil nor for manure. People throw it outside. Let him that has ears to listen, listen.”

25705.label: Luke 15:1
25705.text: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners kept drawing near to him to hear him.

25706.label: Luke 15:2
25706.text: Consequently both the Pharisees and the scribes kept muttering, saying: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

25707.label: Luke 15:3
25707.text: Then he spoke this illustration to them, saying:

25708.label: Luke 15:4
25708.text: “What man of YOU with a hundred sheep, on losing one of them, will not leave the ninety-nine behind in the wilderness and go for the lost one until he finds it?

25709.label: Luke 15:5
25709.text: And when he has found it he puts it upon his shoulders and rejoices.

25710.label: Luke 15:6
25710.text: And when he gets home he calls his friends and his neighbors together, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.’

25711.label: Luke 15:7
25711.text: I tell YOU that thus there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner that repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who have no need of repentance.

25712.label: Luke 15:8
25712.text: “Or what woman with ten drachma coins, if she loses one drachma coin, does not light a lamp and sweep her house and search carefully until she finds it?

25713.label: Luke 15:9
25713.text: And when she has found it she calls the women who are her friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma coin that I lost.’

25714.label: Luke 15:10
25714.text: Thus, I tell YOU, joy arises among the angels of God over one sinner that repents.”

25715.label: Luke 15:11
25715.text: Then he said: “A certain man had two sons.

25716.label: Luke 15:12
25716.text: And the younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the part of the property that falls to my share.’ Then he divided his means of living to them.

25717.label: Luke 15:13
25717.text: Later, after not many days, the younger son gathered all things together and traveled abroad into a distant country, and there squandered his property by living a debauched life.

25718.label: Luke 15:14
25718.text: When he had spent everything, a severe famine occurred throughout that country, and he started to be in need.

25719.label: Luke 15:15
25719.text: He even went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to herd swine.

25720.label: Luke 15:16
25720.text: And he used to desire to be filled with the carob pods which the swine were eating, and no one would give him [anything].

25721.label: Luke 15:17
25721.text: “When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many hired men of my father are abounding with bread, while I am perishing here from famine!

25722.label: Luke 15:18
25722.text: I will rise and journey to my father and say to him: “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

25723.label: Luke 15:19
25723.text: I am no longer worthy of being called your son. Make me as one of your hired men.”’

25724.label: Luke 15:20
25724.text: So he rose and went to his father. While he was yet a long way off, his father caught sight of him and was moved with pity, and he ran and fell upon his neck and tenderly kissed him.

25725.label: Luke 15:21
25725.text: Then the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy of being called your son. Make me as one of your hired men.’

25726.label: Luke 15:22
25726.text: But the father said to his slaves, ‘Quick! bring out a robe, the best one, and clothe him with it, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.

25727.label: Luke 15:23
25727.text: And bring the fattened young bull, slaughter it and let us eat and enjoy ourselves,

25728.label: Luke 15:24
25728.text: because this my son was dead and came to life again; he was lost and was found.’ And they started to enjoy themselves.

25729.label: Luke 15:25
25729.text: “Now his older son was in the field; and as he came and got near the house he heard a music concert and dancing.

25730.label: Luke 15:26
25730.text: So he called one of the servants to him and inquired what these things meant.

25731.label: Luke 15:27
25731.text: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father slaughtered the fattened young bull, because he got him back in good health.’

25732.label: Luke 15:28
25732.text: But he became wrathful and was unwilling to go in. Then his father came out and began to entreat him.

25733.label: Luke 15:29
25733.text: In reply he said to his father, ‘Here it is so many years I have slaved for you and never once did I transgress your commandment, and yet to me you never once gave a kid for me to enjoy myself with my friends.

25734.label: Luke 15:30
25734.text: But as soon as this your son who ate up your means of living with harlots arrived, you slaughtered the fattened young bull for him.’

25735.label: Luke 15:31
25735.text: Then he said to him, ‘Child, you have always been with me, and all the things that are mine are yours;

25736.label: Luke 15:32
25736.text: but we just had to enjoy ourselves and rejoice, because this your brother was dead and came to life, and he was lost and was found.’”

25737.label: Luke 16:1
25737.text: Then he went on to say also to the disciples: “A certain man was rich and he had a steward, and this one was accused to him as handling his goods wastefully.

25738.label: Luke 16:2
25738.text: So he called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Hand in the account of your stewardship, for you can no longer manage the house.’

25739.label: Luke 16:3
25739.text: Then the steward said to himself, ‘What am I to do, seeing that my master will take the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig, I am ashamed to beg.

25740.label: Luke 16:4
25740.text: Ah! I know what I shall do, so that, when I am put out of the stewardship, people will receive me into their homes.’

25741.label: Luke 16:5
25741.text: And calling to him each one of the debtors of his master he proceeded to say to the first, ‘How much are you owing my master?’

25742.label: Luke 16:6
25742.text: He said, ‘A hundred bath measures of olive oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your written agreement back and sit down and quickly write fifty.’

25743.label: Luke 16:7
25743.text: Next, he said to another one, ‘Now you, how much are you owing?’ He said, ‘A hundred cor measures of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your written agreement back and write eighty.’

25744.label: Luke 16:8
25744.text: And his master commended the steward, though unrighteous, because he acted with practical wisdom; for the sons of this system of things are wiser in a practical way toward their own generation than the sons of the light are.

25745.label: Luke 16:9
25745.text: “Also, I say to YOU, Make friends for yourselves by means of the unrighteous riches, so that, when such fail, they may receive YOU into the everlasting dwelling places.

25746.label: Luke 16:10
25746.text: The person faithful in what is least is faithful also in much, and the person unrighteous in what is least is unrighteous also in much.

25747.label: Luke 16:11
25747.text: Therefore, if YOU have not proved yourselves faithful in connection with the unrighteous riches, who will entrust YOU with what is true?

25748.label: Luke 16:12
25748.text: And if YOU have not proved yourselves faithful in connection with what is another’s, who will give YOU what is for yourselves?

25749.label: Luke 16:13
25749.text: No house servant can be a slave to two masters; for, either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will stick to the one and despise the other. YOU cannot be slaves to God and to riches.”

25750.label: Luke 16:14
25750.text: Now the Pharisees, who were money lovers, were listening to all these things, and they began to sneer at him.

25751.label: Luke 16:15
25751.text: Consequently he said to them: “YOU are those who declare yourselves righteous before men, but God knows YOUR hearts; because what is lofty among men is a disgusting thing in God’s sight.

25752.label: Luke 16:16
25752.text: “The Law and the Prophets were until John. From then on the kingdom of God is being declared as good news, and every sort of person is pressing forward toward it.

25753.label: Luke 16:17
25753.text: Indeed, it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one particle of a letter of the Law to go unfulfilled.

25754.label: Luke 16:18
25754.text: “Everyone that divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and he that marries a woman divorced from a husband commits adultery.

25755.label: Luke 16:19
25755.text: “But a certain man was rich, and he used to deck himself with purple and linen, enjoying himself from day to day with magnificence.

25756.label: Luke 16:20
25756.text: But a certain beggar named Lazʹa·rus used to be put at his gate, full of ulcers

25757.label: Luke 16:21
25757.text: and desiring to be filled with the things dropping from the table of the rich man. Yes, too, the dogs would come and lick his ulcers.

25758.label: Luke 16:22
25758.text: Now in course of time the beggar died and he was carried off by the angels to the bosom [position] of Abraham. “Also, the rich man died and was buried.

25759.label: Luke 16:23
25759.text: And in Haʹdes he lifted up his eyes, he existing in torments, and he saw Abraham afar off and Lazʹa·rus in the bosom [position] with him.

25760.label: Luke 16:24
25760.text: So he called and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazʹa·rus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in anguish in this blazing fire.’

25761.label: Luke 16:25
25761.text: But Abraham said, ‘Child, remember that you received in full your good things in your lifetime, but Lazʹa·rus correspondingly the injurious things. Now, however, he is having comfort here but you are in anguish.

25762.label: Luke 16:26
25762.text: And besides all these things, a great chasm has been fixed between us and YOU people, so that those wanting to go over from here to YOU people cannot, neither may people cross over from there to us.’

25763.label: Luke 16:27
25763.text: Then he said, ‘In that event I ask you, father, to send him to the house of my father,

25764.label: Luke 16:28
25764.text: for I have five brothers, in order that he may give them a thorough witness, that they also should not get into this place of torment.’

25765.label: Luke 16:29
25765.text: But Abraham said, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to these.’

25766.label: Luke 16:30
25766.text: Then he said, ‘No, indeed, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them they will repent.’

25767.label: Luke 16:31
25767.text: But he said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.’”

25768.label: Luke 17:1
25768.text: Then he said to his disciples: “It is unavoidable that causes for stumbling should come. Nevertheless, woe to the one through whom they come!

25769.label: Luke 17:2
25769.text: It would be of more advantage to him if a millstone were suspended from his neck and he were thrown into the sea than for him to stumble one of these little ones.

25770.label: Luke 17:3
25770.text: Pay attention to yourselves. If your brother commits a sin give him a rebuke, and if he repents forgive him.

25771.label: Luke 17:4
25771.text: Even if he sins seven times a day against you and he comes back to you seven times, saying, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

25772.label: Luke 17:5
25772.text: Now the apostles said to the Lord: “Give us more faith.”

25773.label: Luke 17:6
25773.text: Then the Lord said: “If YOU had faith the size of a mustard grain, YOU would say to this black mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea!’ and it would obey YOU.

25774.label: Luke 17:7
25774.text: “Who of YOU is there that has a slave plowing or minding the flock who will say to him when he gets in from the field, ‘Come here at once and recline at the table’?

25775.label: Luke 17:8
25775.text: Rather, will he not say to him, ‘Get something ready for me to have my evening meal, and put on an apron and minister to me until I am through eating and drinking, and afterward you can eat and drink’?

25776.label: Luke 17:9
25776.text: He will not feel gratitude to the slave because he did the things assigned, will he?

25777.label: Luke 17:10
25777.text: So YOU, also, when YOU have done all the things assigned to YOU, say, ‘We are good-for-nothing slaves. What we have done is what we ought to have done.’”

25778.label: Luke 17:11
25778.text: And while he was going to Jerusalem he was passing through the midst of Sa·marʹi·a and Galʹi·lee.

25779.label: Luke 17:12
25779.text: And as he was entering into a certain village ten leprous men met him, but they stood up afar off.

25780.label: Luke 17:13
25780.text: And they raised their voices and said: “Jesus, Instructor, have mercy on us!”

25781.label: Luke 17:14
25781.text: And when he got sight of them he said to them: “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” Then as they were going off their cleansing occurred.

25782.label: Luke 17:15
25782.text: One of them, when he saw he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.

25783.label: Luke 17:16
25783.text: And he fell upon his face at [Jesus’] feet, thanking him; furthermore, he was a Sa·marʹi·tan.

25784.label: Luke 17:17
25784.text: In reply Jesus said: “The ten were cleansed, were they not? Where, then, are the other nine?

25785.label: Luke 17:18
25785.text: Were none found that turned back to give glory to God but this man of another nation?”

25786.label: Luke 17:19
25786.text: And he said to him: “Rise and be on your way; your faith has made you well.”

25787.label: Luke 17:20
25787.text: But on being asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them and said: “The kingdom of God is not coming with striking observableness,

25788.label: Luke 17:21
25788.text: neither will people be saying, ‘See here!’ or, ‘There!’ For, look! the kingdom of God is in YOUR midst.”

25789.label: Luke 17:22
25789.text: Then he said to the disciples: “Days will come when YOU will desire to see one of the days of the Son of man but YOU will not see [it].

25790.label: Luke 17:23
25790.text: And people will say to YOU, ‘See there!’ or, ‘See here!’ Do not go out or chase after [them].

25791.label: Luke 17:24
25791.text: For even as the lightning, by its flashing, shines from one part under heaven to another part under heaven, so the Son of man will be.

25792.label: Luke 17:25
25792.text: First, however, he must undergo many sufferings and be rejected by this generation.

25793.label: Luke 17:26
25793.text: Moreover, just as it occurred in the days of Noah, so it will be also in the days of the Son of man:

25794.label: Luke 17:27
25794.text: they were eating, they were drinking, men were marrying, women were being given in marriage, until that day when Noah entered into the ark, and the flood arrived and destroyed them all.

25795.label: Luke 17:28
25795.text: Likewise, just as it occurred in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building.

25796.label: Luke 17:29
25796.text: But on the day that Lot came out of Sodʹom it rained fire and sulphur from heaven and destroyed them all.

25797.label: Luke 17:30
25797.text: The same way it will be on that day when the Son of man is to be revealed.

25798.label: Luke 17:31
25798.text: “On that day let the person that is on the housetop but whose movable things are in the house not come down to pick these up, and the person out in the field, let him likewise not return to the things behind.

25800.label: Luke 17:33
25800.text: Whoever seeks to keep his soul safe for himself will lose it, but whoever loses it will preserve it alive.

25801.label: Luke 17:34
25801.text: I tell YOU, In that night two [men] will be in one bed; the one will be taken along, but the other will be abandoned.

25802.label: Luke 17:35
25802.text: There will be two [women] grinding at the same mill; the one will be taken along, but the other will be abandoned.”

25804.label: Luke 17:37
25804.text: So in response they said to him: “Where, Lord?” He said to them: “Where the body is, there also the eagles will be gathered together.”

25805.label: Luke 18:1
25805.text: Then he went on to tell them an illustration with regard to the need for them always to pray and not to give up,

25806.label: Luke 18:2
25806.text: saying: “In a certain city there was a certain judge that had no fear of God and had no respect for man.

25807.label: Luke 18:3
25807.text: But there was a widow in that city and she kept going to him, saying, ‘See that I get justice from my adversary at law.’

25808.label: Luke 18:4
25808.text: Well, for a while he was unwilling, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Although I do not fear God or respect a man,

25809.label: Luke 18:5
25809.text: at any rate, because of this widow’s continually making me trouble, I will see that she gets justice, so that she will not keep coming and pummeling me to a finish.’”

25810.label: Luke 18:6
25810.text: Then the Lord said: “HEAR what the judge, although unrighteous, said!

25811.label: Luke 18:7
25811.text: Certainly, then, shall not God cause justice to be done for his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night, even though he is long-suffering toward them?

25812.label: Luke 18:8
25812.text: I tell YOU, He will cause justice to be done to them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man arrives, will he really find the faith on the earth?”

25813.label: Luke 18:9
25813.text: But he spoke this illustration also to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and who considered the rest as nothing:

25814.label: Luke 18:10
25814.text: “Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

25815.label: Luke 18:11
25815.text: The Pharisee stood and began to pray these things to himself, ‘O God, I thank you I am not as the rest of men, extortioners, unrighteous, adulterers, or even as this tax collector.

25816.label: Luke 18:12
25816.text: I fast twice a week, I give the tenth of all things I acquire.’

25817.label: Luke 18:13
25817.text: But the tax collector standing at a distance was not willing even to raise his eyes heavenward, but kept beating his breast, saying, ‘O God, be gracious to me a sinner.’

25818.label: Luke 18:14
25818.text: I tell YOU, This man went down to his home proved more righteous than that man; because everyone that exalts himself will be humiliated, but he that humbles himself will be exalted.”

25819.label: Luke 18:15
25819.text: Now people began to bring him also their infants for him to touch these; but on seeing it the disciples began to reprimand them.

25820.label: Luke 18:16
25820.text: However, Jesus called the [infants] to him, saying: “Let the young children come to me, and do not try to stop them. For the kingdom of God belongs to suchlike ones.

25821.label: Luke 18:17
25821.text: Truly I say to YOU, Whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a young child will by no means get into it.”

25822.label: Luke 18:18
25822.text: And a certain ruler questioned him, saying: “Good Teacher, by doing what shall I inherit everlasting life?”

25823.label: Luke 18:19
25823.text: Jesus said to him: “Why do you call me good? Nobody is good, except one, God.

25824.label: Luke 18:20
25824.text: You know the commandments, ‘Do not commit adultery, Do not murder, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honor your father and mother.’”

25825.label: Luke 18:21
25825.text: Then he said: “All these I have kept from youth on.”

25826.label: Luke 18:22
25826.text: After hearing that, Jesus said to him: “There is yet one thing lacking about you: Sell all the things you have and distribute to poor people, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come be my follower.”

25827.label: Luke 18:23
25827.text: When he heard this, he became deeply grieved, for he was very rich.

25828.label: Luke 18:24
25828.text: Jesus looked at him and said: “How difficult a thing it will be for those having money to make their way into the kingdom of God!

25829.label: Luke 18:25
25829.text: It is easier, in fact, for a camel to get through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich man to get into the kingdom of God.”

25830.label: Luke 18:26
25830.text: Those who heard this said: “Who possibly can be saved?”

25831.label: Luke 18:27
25831.text: He said: “The things impossible with men are possible with God.”

25832.label: Luke 18:28
25832.text: But Peter said: “Look! We have left our own things and followed you.”

25833.label: Luke 18:29
25833.text: He said to them: “Truly I say to YOU, There is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God

25834.label: Luke 18:30
25834.text: who will not in any way get many times more in this period of time, and in the coming system of things everlasting life.”

25835.label: Luke 18:31
25835.text: Then he took the twelve aside and said to them: “Look! We are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written by means of the prophets as to the Son of man will be completed.

25836.label: Luke 18:32
25836.text: For instance, he will be delivered up to [men of] the nations and will be made fun of and be treated insolently and spit upon;

25837.label: Luke 18:33
25837.text: and after scourging him they will kill him, but on the third day he will rise.”

25838.label: Luke 18:34
25838.text: However, they did not get the meaning of any of these things; but this utterance was hidden from them, and they were not knowing the things said.

25839.label: Luke 18:35
25839.text: Now as he was getting near to Jerʹi·cho a certain blind man was sitting beside the road begging.

25840.label: Luke 18:36
25840.text: Because he heard a crowd moving through he began to inquire what this might mean.

25841.label: Luke 18:37
25841.text: They reported to him: “Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ is passing by!”

25842.label: Luke 18:38
25842.text: At that he cried out, saying: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

25843.label: Luke 18:39
25843.text: And those going in advance began to tell him sternly to keep quiet, but that much more he kept shouting: “Son of David, have mercy on me.”

25844.label: Luke 18:40
25844.text: Then Jesus stood still and commanded the [man] to be led to him. After he got near, [Jesus] asked him:

25845.label: Luke 18:41
25845.text: “What do you want me to do for you?” He said: “Lord, let me recover sight.”

25846.label: Luke 18:42
25846.text: So Jesus said to him: “Recover your sight; your faith has made you well.”

25847.label: Luke 18:43
25847.text: And instantly he recovered sight, and he began to follow him, glorifying God. Also, all the people, at seeing [it], gave praise to God.

25848.label: Luke 19:1
25848.text: And he entered Jerʹi·cho and was going through.

25849.label: Luke 19:2
25849.text: Now here there was a man called by the name Zac·chaeʹus; and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

25850.label: Luke 19:3
25850.text: Well, he was seeking to see who this Jesus was, but he could not for the crowd, because he was small in size.

25851.label: Luke 19:4
25851.text: So he ran ahead to an advance position and climbed a fig-mulberry tree in order to see him, because he was about to go through that way.

25852.label: Luke 19:5
25852.text: Now when Jesus got to the place, he looked up and said to him: “Zac·chaeʹus, hurry and get down, for today I must stay in your house.”

25853.label: Luke 19:6
25853.text: With that he hurried and got down and with rejoicing he received him as guest.

25854.label: Luke 19:7
25854.text: But when they saw [it], they all fell to muttering, saying: “With a man that is a sinner he went in to lodge.”

25855.label: Luke 19:8
25855.text: But Zac·chaeʹus stood up and said to the Lord: “Look! The half of my belongings, Lord, I am giving to the poor, and whatever I extorted from anyone by false accusation I am restoring fourfold.”

25856.label: Luke 19:9
25856.text: At this Jesus said to him: “This day salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.

25857.label: Luke 19:10
25857.text: For the Son of man came to seek and to save what was lost.”

25858.label: Luke 19:11
25858.text: While they were listening to these things he spoke in addition an illustration, because he was near Jerusalem and they were imagining that the kingdom of God was going to display itself instantly.

25859.label: Luke 19:12
25859.text: Therefore he said: “A certain man of noble birth traveled to a distant land to secure kingly power for himself and to return.

25860.label: Luke 19:13
25860.text: Calling ten slaves of his he gave them ten miʹnas and told them, ‘Do business till I come.’

25861.label: Luke 19:14
25861.text: But his citizens hated him and sent out a body of ambassadors after him, to say, ‘We do not want this [man] to become king over us.’

25862.label: Luke 19:15
25862.text: “Eventually when he got back after having secured the kingly power, he commanded to be called to him these slaves to whom he had given the silver money, in order to ascertain what they had gained by business activity.

25863.label: Luke 19:16
25863.text: Then the first one presented himself, saying, ‘Lord, your miʹna gained ten miʹnas.’

25864.label: Luke 19:17
25864.text: So he said to him, ‘Well done, good slave! Because in a very small matter you have proved yourself faithful, hold authority over ten cities.’

25865.label: Luke 19:18
25865.text: Now the second came, saying, ‘Your miʹna, Lord, made five miʹnas.’

25866.label: Luke 19:19
25866.text: He said to this one also, ‘You, too, be in charge of five cities.’

25867.label: Luke 19:20
25867.text: But a different one came, saying, ‘Lord, here is your miʹna, that I kept laid away in a cloth.

25868.label: Luke 19:21
25868.text: You see, I was in fear of you, because you are a harsh man; you take up what you did not deposit and you reap what you did not sow.’

25869.label: Luke 19:22
25869.text: He said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked slave. You knew, did you, that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?

25870.label: Luke 19:23
25870.text: Hence why is it you did not put my silver money in a bank? Then on my arrival I would have collected it with interest.’

25871.label: Luke 19:24
25871.text: “With that he said to those standing by, ‘Take the miʹna from him and give it to him that has the ten miʹnas.’

25872.label: Luke 19:25
25872.text: But they said to him, ‘Lord, he has ten miʹnas!’—

25873.label: Luke 19:26
25873.text: ‘I say to YOU, To everyone that has, more will be given; but from the one that does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

25874.label: Luke 19:27
25874.text: Moreover, these enemies of mine that did not want me to become king over them BRING here and slaughter them before me.’”

25875.label: Luke 19:28
25875.text: So, after he had said these things, he began to go on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

25876.label: Luke 19:29
25876.text: And when he got near to Bethʹpha·ge and Bethʹa·ny at the mountain called Mount of Olives, he sent forth two of the disciples,

25877.label: Luke 19:30
25877.text: saying: “Go into the village that is within sight of YOU, and in it after YOU pass in YOU will find a colt tied, on which none of mankind ever sat. Loose it and bring it.

25878.label: Luke 19:31
25878.text: But if anyone asks YOU, ‘Why is it YOU are loosing it?’ YOU must speak in this way, ‘The Lord needs it.’”

25879.label: Luke 19:32
25879.text: So those who were sent forth departed and found it just as he said to them.

25880.label: Luke 19:33
25880.text: But as they were loosing the colt the owners of it said to them: “Why are YOU loosing the colt?”

25882.label: Luke 19:35
25882.text: And they led it to Jesus, and they threw their outer garments upon the colt and set Jesus upon [it].

25883.label: Luke 19:36
25883.text: As he moved along they kept spreading their outer garments on the road.

25884.label: Luke 19:37
25884.text: As soon as he got near the road down the Mount of Olives all the multitude of the disciples started to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice concerning all the powerful works they had seen,

25885.label: Luke 19:38
25885.text: saying: “Blessed is the One coming as the King in Jehovah’s name! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest places!”

25886.label: Luke 19:39
25886.text: However, some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him: “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”

25887.label: Luke 19:40
25887.text: But in reply he said: “I tell YOU, If these remained silent, the stones would cry out.”

25888.label: Luke 19:41
25888.text: And when he got nearby, he viewed the city and wept over it,

25889.label: Luke 19:42
25889.text: saying: “If you, even you, had discerned in this day the things having to do with peace—but now they have been hid from your eyes.

25890.label: Luke 19:43
25890.text: Because the days will come upon you when your enemies will build around you a fortification with pointed stakes and will encircle you and distress you from every side,

25891.label: Luke 19:44
25891.text: and they will dash you and your children within you to the ground, and they will not leave a stone upon a stone in you, because you did not discern the time of your being inspected.”

25892.label: Luke 19:45
25892.text: And he entered into the temple and started to throw out those who were selling,

25893.label: Luke 19:46
25893.text: saying to them: “It is written, ‘And my house will be a house of prayer,’ but YOU made it a cave of robbers.”

25894.label: Luke 19:47
25894.text: Furthermore, he went teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the principal ones of the people were seeking to destroy him;

25895.label: Luke 19:48
25895.text: and yet they did not find the effective thing for them to do, for the people one and all kept hanging onto him to hear him.

25896.label: Luke 20:1
25896.text: On one of the days while he was teaching the people in the temple and declaring the good news, the chief priests and the scribes with the older men came near,

25897.label: Luke 20:2
25897.text: and they spoke up, saying to him: “Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is that gave you this authority.”

25898.label: Luke 20:3
25898.text: In reply he said to them: “I will also ask YOU a question, and YOU tell me:

25899.label: Luke 20:4
25899.text: Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men?”

25900.label: Luke 20:5
25900.text: Then among themselves they drew conclusions, saying: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why is it YOU did not believe him?’

25901.label: Luke 20:6
25901.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ the people one and all will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.”

25902.label: Luke 20:7
25902.text: So they replied that they did not know its source.

25903.label: Luke 20:8
25903.text: And Jesus said to them: “Neither am I telling YOU by what authority I do these things.”

25904.label: Luke 20:9
25904.text: Then he started to tell the people this illustration: “A man planted a vineyard and let it out to cultivators, and he traveled abroad for considerable time.

25905.label: Luke 20:10
25905.text: But in due season he sent out a slave to the cultivators, that they might give him some of the fruit of the vineyard. The cultivators, however, sent him away empty, after beating him up.

25906.label: Luke 20:11
25906.text: But he repeated and sent them a different slave. That one also they beat up and dishonored and sent away empty.

25907.label: Luke 20:12
25907.text: Yet again he sent a third; this one also they wounded and threw out.

25908.label: Luke 20:13
25908.text: At this the owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my son the beloved. Likely they will respect this one.’

25909.label: Luke 20:14
25909.text: When the cultivators caught sight of him they went reasoning with one another, saying, ‘This is the heir; let us kill him, that the inheritance may become ours.’

25910.label: Luke 20:15
25910.text: With that they threw him outside the vineyard and killed him. What, therefore, will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

25911.label: Luke 20:16
25911.text: He will come and destroy these cultivators and will give the vineyard to others.” On hearing [this] they said: “Never may that happen!”

25912.label: Luke 20:17
25912.text: But he looked upon them and said: “What, then, does this that is written mean, ‘The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the chief cornerstone’?

25913.label: Luke 20:18
25913.text: Everyone falling upon that stone will be shattered. As for anyone upon whom it falls, it will pulverize him.”

25914.label: Luke 20:19
25914.text: The scribes and the chief priests now sought to get their hands on him in that very hour, but they feared the people; for they perceived that he spoke this illustration with them in mind.

25915.label: Luke 20:20
25915.text: And, after observing him closely, they sent out men secretly hired to pretend that they were righteous, in order that they might catch him in speech, so as to turn him over to the government and to the authority of the governor.

25916.label: Luke 20:21
25916.text: And they questioned him, saying: “Teacher, we know you speak and teach correctly and show no partiality, but you teach the way of God in line with truth:

25917.label: Luke 20:22
25917.text: Is it lawful for us to pay tax to Caesar or not?”

25918.label: Luke 20:23
25918.text: But he detected their cunning and said to them:

25919.label: Luke 20:24
25919.text: “Show me a de·narʹi·us. Whose image and inscription does it have?” They said: “Caesar’s.”

25920.label: Luke 20:25
25920.text: He said to them: “By all means, then, pay back Caesar’s things to Caesar, but God’s things to God.”

25921.label: Luke 20:26
25921.text: Well, they were not able to catch him in this saying before the people, but, in amazement at his answer, they said nothing.

25922.label: Luke 20:27
25922.text: However, some of the Sadducees, those who say there is no resurrection, came up and questioned him,

25923.label: Luke 20:28
25923.text: saying: “Teacher, Moses wrote us, ‘If a man’s brother dies having a wife, but this one remained childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring from her for his brother.’

25924.label: Luke 20:29
25924.text: Accordingly there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife and died childless.

25926.label: Luke 20:31
25926.text: and the third took her. Likewise even the seven: they did not leave children behind, but died off.

25928.label: Luke 20:33
25928.text: Consequently, in the resurrection, of which one of them does she become [the] wife? For the seven got her as wife.”

25929.label: Luke 20:34
25929.text: Jesus said to them: “The children of this system of things marry and are given in marriage,

25930.label: Luke 20:35
25930.text: but those who have been counted worthy of gaining that system of things and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.

25931.label: Luke 20:36
25931.text: In fact, neither can they die anymore, for they are like the angels, and they are God’s children by being children of the resurrection.

25932.label: Luke 20:37
25932.text: But that the dead are raised up even Moses disclosed, in the account about the thornbush, when he calls Jehovah ‘the God of Abraham and God of Isaac and God of Jacob.’

25933.label: Luke 20:38
25933.text: He is a God, not of the dead, but of the living, for they are all living to him.”

25934.label: Luke 20:39
25934.text: In response some of the scribes said: “Teacher, you spoke well.”

25935.label: Luke 20:40
25935.text: For no longer did they have the courage to ask him a single question.

25936.label: Luke 20:41
25936.text: In turn he said to them: “How is it they say that the Christ is David’s son?

25937.label: Luke 20:42
25937.text: For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘Jehovah said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand

25938.label: Luke 20:43
25938.text: until I place your enemies as a stool for your feet.’

25939.label: Luke 20:44
25939.text: David, therefore, calls him ‘Lord’; so how is he his son?”

25940.label: Luke 20:45
25940.text: Then, while all the people were listening he said to the disciples:

25941.label: Luke 20:46
25941.text: “Look out for the scribes who desire to walk around in robes and like greetings in the marketplaces and front seats in the synagogues and most prominent places at evening meals,

25942.label: Luke 20:47
25942.text: and who devour the houses of the widows and for a pretext make long prayers. These will receive a heavier judgment.”

25943.label: Luke 21:1
25943.text: Now as he looked up he saw the rich dropping their gifts into the treasury chests.

25944.label: Luke 21:2
25944.text: Then he saw a certain needy widow drop two small coins of very little value there,

25945.label: Luke 21:3
25945.text: and he said: “I tell YOU truthfully, This widow, although poor, dropped in more than they all did.

25946.label: Luke 21:4
25946.text: For all these dropped in gifts out of their surplus, but this [woman] out of her want dropped in all the means of living she had.”

25947.label: Luke 21:5
25947.text: Later, as certain ones were speaking concerning the temple, how it was adorned with fine stones and dedicated things,

25948.label: Luke 21:6
25948.text: he said: “As for these things that YOU are beholding, the days will come in which not a stone upon a stone will be left here and not be thrown down.”

25949.label: Luke 21:7
25949.text: Then they questioned him, saying: “Teacher, when will these things actually be, and what will be the sign when these things are destined to occur?”

25950.label: Luke 21:8
25950.text: He said: “Look out that YOU are not misled; for many will come on the basis of my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The due time has approached.’ Do not go after them.

25951.label: Luke 21:9
25951.text: Furthermore, when YOU hear of wars and disorders, do not be terrified. For these things must occur first, but the end does not [occur] immediately.”

25952.label: Luke 21:10
25952.text: Then he went on to say to them: “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;

25953.label: Luke 21:11
25953.text: and there will be great earthquakes, and in one place after another pestilences and food shortages; and there will be fearful sights and from heaven great signs.

25954.label: Luke 21:12
25954.text: “But before all these things people will lay their hands upon YOU and persecute YOU, delivering YOU up to the synagogues and prisons, YOU being haled before kings and governors for the sake of my name.

25955.label: Luke 21:13
25955.text: It will turn out to YOU for a witness.

25956.label: Luke 21:14
25956.text: Therefore settle it in YOUR hearts not to rehearse beforehand how to make YOUR defense,

25957.label: Luke 21:15
25957.text: for I will give YOU a mouth and wisdom, which all YOUR opposers together will not be able to resist or dispute.

25958.label: Luke 21:16
25958.text: Moreover, YOU will be delivered up even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of YOU to death;

25959.label: Luke 21:17
25959.text: and YOU will be objects of hatred by all people because of my name.

25960.label: Luke 21:18
25960.text: And yet not a hair of YOUR heads will by any means perish.

25961.label: Luke 21:19
25961.text: By endurance on YOUR part YOU will acquire YOUR souls.

25962.label: Luke 21:20
25962.text: “Furthermore, when YOU see Jerusalem surrounded by encamped armies, then know that the desolating of her has drawn near.

25963.label: Luke 21:21
25963.text: Then let those in Ju·deʹa begin fleeing to the mountains, and let those in the midst of her withdraw, and let those in the country places not enter into her;

25964.label: Luke 21:22
25964.text: because these are days for meting out justice, that all the things written may be fulfilled.

25965.label: Luke 21:23
25965.text: Woe to the pregnant women and the ones suckling a baby in those days! For there will be great necessity upon the land and wrath on this people;

25966.label: Luke 21:24
25966.text: and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled on by the nations, until the appointed times of the nations are fulfilled.

25967.label: Luke 21:25
25967.text: “Also, there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth anguish of nations, not knowing the way out because of the roaring of the sea and [its] agitation,

25968.label: Luke 21:26
25968.text: while men become faint out of fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited earth; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

25969.label: Luke 21:27
25969.text: And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

25970.label: Luke 21:28
25970.text: But as these things start to occur, raise yourselves erect and lift YOUR heads up, because YOUR deliverance is getting near.”

25971.label: Luke 21:29
25971.text: With that he spoke an illustration to them: “Note the fig tree and all the other trees:

25972.label: Luke 21:30
25972.text: When they are already in the bud, by observing it YOU know for yourselves that now the summer is near.

25973.label: Luke 21:31
25973.text: In this way YOU also, when YOU see these things occurring, know that the kingdom of God is near.

25974.label: Luke 21:32
25974.text: Truly I say to YOU, This generation will by no means pass away until all things occur.

25975.label: Luke 21:33
25975.text: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.

25976.label: Luke 21:34
25976.text: “But pay attention to yourselves that YOUR hearts never become weighed down with overeating and heavy drinking and anxieties of life, and suddenly that day be instantly upon YOU

25977.label: Luke 21:35
25977.text: as a snare. For it will come in upon all those dwelling upon the face of all the earth.

25978.label: Luke 21:36
25978.text: Keep awake, then, all the time making supplication that YOU may succeed in escaping all these things that are destined to occur, and in standing before the Son of man.”

25979.label: Luke 21:37
25979.text: So by day he would be teaching in the temple, but by night he would go out and lodge on the mountain called the Mount of Olives.

25980.label: Luke 21:38
25980.text: And all the people would come early in the day to him in the temple to hear him.

25981.label: Luke 22:1
25981.text: Now the festival of the unfermented cakes, the so-called Passover, was getting near.

25982.label: Luke 22:2
25982.text: Also, the chief priests and the scribes were seeking the effective way for them to get rid of him, for they were in fear of the people.

25983.label: Luke 22:3
25983.text: But Satan entered into Judas, the one called Is·carʹi·ot, who was numbered among the twelve;

25984.label: Luke 22:4
25984.text: and he went off and talked with the chief priests and [temple] captains about the effective way to betray him to them.

25985.label: Luke 22:5
25985.text: Well, they rejoiced and agreed to give him silver money.

25986.label: Luke 22:6
25986.text: So he consented, and he began to seek a good opportunity to betray him to them without a crowd around.

25987.label: Luke 22:7
25987.text: The day of the unfermented cakes now arrived, on which the passover [victim] must be sacrificed;

25988.label: Luke 22:8
25988.text: and he dispatched Peter and John, saying: “Go and get the passover ready for us to eat.”

25989.label: Luke 22:9
25989.text: They said to him: “Where do you want us to get [it] ready?”

25990.label: Luke 22:10
25990.text: He said to them: “Look! When YOU enter into the city a man carrying an earthenware vessel of water will meet YOU. Follow him into the house into which he enters.

25991.label: Luke 22:11
25991.text: And YOU must say to the landlord of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you: “Where is the guest room in which I may eat the passover with my disciples?”’

25992.label: Luke 22:12
25992.text: And that [man] will show YOU a large upper room furnished. Get [it] ready there.”

25993.label: Luke 22:13
25993.text: So they departed and found it just as he had said to them, and they got the passover ready.

25994.label: Luke 22:14
25994.text: At length when the hour came, he reclined at the table, and the apostles with him.

25995.label: Luke 22:15
25995.text: And he said to them: “I have greatly desired to eat this passover with YOU before I suffer;

25996.label: Luke 22:16
25996.text: for I tell YOU, I will not eat it again until it becomes fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”

25997.label: Luke 22:17
25997.text: And, accepting a cup, he gave thanks and said: “Take this and pass it from one to the other among yourselves;

25998.label: Luke 22:18
25998.text: for I tell YOU, From now on I will not drink again from the product of the vine until the kingdom of God arrives.”

25999.label: Luke 22:19
25999.text: Also, he took a loaf, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying: “This means my body which is to be given in YOUR behalf. Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”

26000.label: Luke 22:20
26000.text: Also, the cup in the same way after they had the evening meal, he saying: “This cup means the new covenant by virtue of my blood, which is to be poured out in YOUR behalf.

26001.label: Luke 22:21
26001.text: “But, look! the hand of my betrayer is with me at the table.

26002.label: Luke 22:22
26002.text: Because the Son of man is going his way according to what is marked out; all the same, woe to that man through whom he is betrayed!”

26003.label: Luke 22:23
26003.text: So they started to discuss among themselves the question of which of them would really be the one that was about to do this.

26004.label: Luke 22:24
26004.text: However, there also arose a heated dispute among them over which one of them seemed to be greatest.

26005.label: Luke 22:25
26005.text: But he said to them: “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those having authority over them are called Benefactors.

26006.label: Luke 22:26
